decisions.title: CBongo/game-music-extraction
decisions.reason: Primary README and system directories establish a coherent multi-system music-sequence extraction and code-analysis project; directories are retained within the root scope rather than split into speculative subprojects.

decisions.title: ajoneil/morepork
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes reusable execution-trace capture, query, comparison and visualization across five legacy emulator families, directly supporting software archaeology.

decisions.title: amypurple/AmyStudio
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes a runnable browser-based ColecoVision development environment with its own Z80-oriented language, compiler, assembler, runtime, examples and embedded test/debug emulator.

decisions.title: plasticbugs/mrdoarcade
decisions.reason: Primary README and shared assembly source establish a substantial ColecoVision fan conversion built from a documented Captain Cosmos disassembly, with five reproducible ROM variants and real-hardware/emulator use.

decisions.title: mstan/SuperMarioBrosNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Fully playable native title port with documented all-world coverage and a bounded demo nondeterminism caveat.

decisions.title: mstan/DuckHuntNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Playable native title port with a documented mouse-backed Zapper implementation.

decisions.title: mstan/DrMarioNesRecomp
decisions.reason: Playable native title port with explicitly bounded one-player and regional-ROM validation.

decisions.title: mstan/LegendOfZeldaNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port with explicit overworld, dungeon and missing-dispatch validation.

decisions.title: mstan/FaxanaduRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port tested from title screen through credits, without overstating exhaustive coverage.

decisions.title: mstan/YoshiNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port with documented one-player, two-player and demo coverage.

decisions.title: mstan/YoshisCookieRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port with one-player and versus testing plus zero-divergence oracle comparison against Nestopia.

decisions.title: mstan/Megaman3NESRecomp
decisions.reason: Distinct work-in-progress native title port whose README bounds support to title/select and early-stage gameplay.

decisions.title: mstan/GumshoeNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Playable end-to-end native title port with mouse-backed Zapper support and one documented cosmetic HUD defect.

decisions.title: drhelius/Gearsystem
decisions.reason: Fresh SG-1000/SC-3000 code search resolved to the already indexed Gearsystem emulator/debugger record; it is not a new project.

decisions.title: drhelius/Gearcoleco
decisions.reason: Fresh ColecoVision code search resolved to the already indexed Gearcoleco emulator/debugger record; it is not a new project.

decisions.title: ocornut/meka
decisions.reason: Fresh Sega 8-bit/ColecoVision code search resolved to the already indexed MEKA emulator record; it is not a new project.

decisions.title: Adventure — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The author states this is a conversion of Joel D. Park's existing commented disassembly and adds essentially no new analysis; do not count the conversion as an independent reverse-engineering project.

decisions.title: Super Mario Bros. — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The author ports doppelganger's existing disassembly and says he has not meaningfully modified the original analysis. Pattern-table visualizers are useful but this is not a separate original game disassembly.

decisions.title: Applesoft BASIC — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The ROM collection identifies this as a conversion of Bob Sander-Cederlof's pre-existing S-C Documentor disassembly; the converted listing is not counted separately. His underlying work remains a potential independent lead.

decisions.title: Super Serial Card firmware — manual conversion
decisions.reason: The ROM index explicitly describes the SourceGen SSC listing as ported from Apple's published firmware source in the installation manual, rather than a separate reconstruction.

decisions.title: Selected Apple II monitor ROMs — published-listing conversions
decisions.reason: The original, autostart, unenhanced IIe and original 16KB IIc monitor listings are described as faithful SourceGen reproductions of published Apple sources with little added commentary. This does not cover James Lewis's expanded 32KB IIc work, independent monitor analysis elsewhere, or James Davis's separate full-ROM project.

decisions.title: Apple IIe 80-column firmware — manual conversion
decisions.reason: The listing says its labels and comments come from Apple's published 80-Column Firmware Listing and describes itself as a fairly direct translation, so this SourceGen copy is not a separate original disassembly.

decisions.title: Apple II DOS 3.3 original-source archive
decisions.reason: Listed under original source listings in the SourceGen outbound index. The repository preserves original DOS 3.3 source and reference material; inspect its own annotations before claiming a distinct reverse-engineering project.

decisions.title: Robotron: 2084 (Atari 7800) — imported disassembly
decisions.reason: The listing's header attributes the Atari 7800 disassembly to Dan Boris with additional work by Scott T, while the enclosing repository documents a separate Apple II Robotron project. Resolve the credited original author's current source before cataloguing a canonical Atari 7800 research record.

decisions.title: jotd666/berzerk
decisions.reason: The sole Berzerk Z80 listing credits Scott Tunstall as its reverser, and the fuller canonical ScottTunstall/Berzerk repository is available. JOTD’s copied file has no independently evidenced Amiga translation; follow the original author for this arcade analysis.

decisions.title: jotd666/super_pacman
decisions.reason: Project-specific 6809 disassembly qualifies as arcade analysis. The README describes Mappy and the Amiga makefile references a missing super_pacman.68k, so no Super Pac-Man Amiga port or working build is claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/digdug
decisions.reason: Copied Dig Dug II README is superseded by the game-specific Dig Dug Z80 listing and Amiga assembly, with build/playability still unknown.

decisions.title: jotd666/rolling_thunder
decisions.reason: Copied Jail Break README does not describe this repository, but dual 6809/MCU listings, a distinct Rolling Thunder Amiga driver and TODO justify a work-in-progress record without build or playability claims.

decisions.title: jotd666/tiger_heli
decisions.reason: Project-specific Z80 disassembly qualifies as arcade analysis. README describes Jail Break, Amiga code describes Commando and makefile Dig Dug 2; no Tiger Heli Amiga port is claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/bosconian
decisions.reason: Copied Rally-X README is superseded by Bosconian Z80 listing and Bosconian-specific Amiga driver work; no playable port claim.

decisions.title: jotd666/mrdo
decisions.reason: Copied Jail Break README is superseded by Mr. Do! Z80 listing and Amiga-specific sprite/high-score code; predecessor template remains acknowledged.

decisions.title: jotd666/jungle_king
decisions.reason: A 256 KB Z80 listing and post-processing script qualify as an arcade disassembly; repository has no Amiga code, so an Amiga conversion is not claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/jrpacman500
decisions.reason: The 15 KB screenshot-to-68000-data conversion script is concrete Amiga development tooling, but the repository has only an assets directory and no generated src tree, game source or working build.

decisions.title: jotd666/marble_madness_2
decisions.reason: A 27 KB C RAM-dump renderer and graphics conversion script qualify as arcade video analysis. The Amiga slave and TODO lack completed ROM patching and tile/sprite ripping, so the record does not claim a playable Amiga port.

decisions.title: jotd666/amitools
decisions.reason: Fork of existing Amiga tools; no distinct JOTD reverse-engineering work established.

decisions.title: jotd666/mame
decisions.reason: MAME fork; no standalone Amiga/ST reconstruction demonstrated.

decisions.title: jotd666/Musashi
decisions.reason: 68000 emulator fork; review upstream rather than cataloguing an unverified duplicate.

decisions.title: jotd666/musashi040
decisions.reason: 68000 emulator fork; review upstream rather than cataloguing an unverified duplicate.

decisions.title: jotd666/gods-deluxe
decisions.reason: Primary Gods Deluxe README documents a substantial beta behavioral remake of the Amiga/Sega game, including observed differences and incomplete level coverage.

decisions.title: jotd666/supercars3
decisions.reason: Project readme.txt documents a substantial playable Super Cars I/II remake and original circuits with known AI/physics differences.

decisions.title: jotd666/pbmplus
decisions.reason: General image utility suite, not a distinct Amiga/ST reverse-engineering target.

decisions.title: jotd666/misctools
decisions.reason: README describes general-purpose Python home/work command-line scripts; grepbin alone does not establish a distinct Amiga/ST research project.

decisions.title: BLACK ICE — original Atari STE game
decisions.reason: Project-specific README explicitly says BLACK ICE is original homebrew built using lessons from the workspace, not a reconstruction or reverse-engineering project. Its Hatari-tested 1 MB STE target is useful development context but does not warrant a catalogue entry.

decisions.title: Into The Eagle’s Nest — misattributed Amiga/Atari ST entry
decisions.reason: The second catalogue entry described this same repository as a partial Amiga/Atari ST reconstruction. Its README and 68000 source establish only an Amiga disassembly. Merged the duplicate into the existing Amiga record and removed the unsupported Atari ST attribution.

decisions.title: The Air Dirt Demo
decisions.reason: README identifies full original assembler source for the group’s own 1996 Falcon demo, with no binary-to-source recovery claim.

decisions.title: The Ultimate Fake
decisions.reason: README identifies full assembler source for the group’s own 1998 ST demo; original-source publication does not itself establish reconstruction.

decisions.title: Xmas Card 97
decisions.reason: README identifies full assembler source for the group’s own 1997 Falcon demo, without a disassembly/reconstruction claim.

decisions.title: ST Floormat
decisions.reason: README identifies the original source and an old source version of the group’s own demo; the Falcon hardware requirement is not evidence of reverse engineering.

decisions.title: Dadplazz
decisions.reason: README identifies full original Falcon demo source and documented build instructions; no binary-to-source reconstruction is described.

decisions.title: RAWTex — planned Amiga/ST planar support
decisions.reason: README says Amiga and Atari ST planar export is planned, while current indexed chunky output primarily targets other architectures; revisit if support lands.

decisions.title: ProTrekkr
decisions.reason: Maintained modern music tracker and heavily modified NoiseTrekker derivative, but README does not establish a distinct Amiga/ST reverse-engineering subject or core disassembly/debugging tool.

decisions.title: STTRANS Atari ST-Book transfer research
decisions.reason: Original STTRANS.PRG, Ghidra project and substantive Python serial companion provide concrete STBook transfer protocol work; no reconstructed executable is claimed.

decisions.title: Starflight Atari ST analysis
decisions.reason: Ghidra project and BTX, AGO and OMEGA Python asset readers substantiate Atari ST binary and format analysis, without claiming a playable Starflight rebuild.

decisions.title: Think & Work Atari ST original-source port
decisions.reason: Author explicitly describes writing this Atari ST game from scratch from the Atari XL game levels and publishing its own original 68k source. No reverse-engineered binary or recovered-source work is established.

decisions.title: TurboAss Atari ST assembler original source
decisions.reason: Publishes the author’s original Atari ST assembler, editor and debugger source rather than independent recovery of a binary or a reconstructed legacy codebase.

decisions.title: AtariDocumentation official manual conversions
decisions.reason: Transcriptions and OCR/text conversions of Atari documentation. This is a document source archive rather than an independent software reverse-engineering subject.

decisions.title: Atari_ST_Sources original-source archive
decisions.reason: Large collection of existing Atari ST assembly and C source trees. The archive alone does not establish a distinct binary-to-source reconstruction project; review a specific contained project separately if authored reverse-engineering evidence appears.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/4489_byteloader
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this as a fork of 4489/4489_byteloader; copied README credits upstream and does not establish a separately documented disassembly. The Infinite Dreams README cites this loader in its later single-disk adaptation.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/amigaprogramming
decisions.reason: Original Amiga 68000 programming examples, without a documented recovered historic binary or reverse-engineered target.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/TTEDiskBuilder-netcore
decisions.reason: README identifies a .NET Core port of h0ffman’s existing ADF disk builder for VS Code; a useful development utility, but no separate reconstructed historical format or subject analysis is demonstrated.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/modprocessor
decisions.reason: Modern ProTracker sample recompression experiment for the author’s demo adaptation; README describes an untested original support utility, not a historic binary or format reconstruction.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/HardwareKeyboardReader
decisions.reason: README describes new Amiga 500 hardware keyboard library code and an in-progress VS Code example, not a reverse-engineered legacy software subject.

decisions.title: Championship Manager 93 folder
decisions.reason: Championship Manager 93 folder contains a game executable/data and patched binary but no distinct source reconstruction or analysis code. The documented Italia reconstruction is already catalogued; a second project for this binary folder would misstate its evidence.

decisions.title: DELA Eprommer reverse engineering
decisions.reason: Primary work reconstructs an Amiga expansion peripheral circuit and PAL equations, while its CLI is newly written to operate that hardware. It does not reconstruct legacy software within the tracker’s software-archaeology scope.

decisions.title: Tearaway Thomas partial reimplementation
decisions.reason: Packed/unpacked dumps and the Python DHp2 unpacker substantiate Amiga game data analysis; broader playability or full game reconstruction is not claimed.

decisions.title: cyxx/another_js
decisions.reason: The browser engine interprets Another World VM opcodes with DOS game data; promoted under DOS origin. Its Amiga palette option alone does not establish Amiga disk compatibility.

decisions.title: cyxx/hode
decisions.reason: A substantial Heart of Darkness engine reimplementation uses Windows demo/CD resource files; promoted under the Windows source platform without an Amiga or Atari ST claim.

decisions.title: nitecrwl
decisions.reason: Author labels the Atari ST game decompiled; gameplay C++, GEM AES/VDI code and cross-build Makefile substantiate source recovery. Original binary identity, matching and runtime verification remain unknown.

decisions.title: amiga_reconstructed
decisions.reason: Three named Amiga intros/trainers from this collection are already catalogued. Remaining directories have not been individually matched to a specific binary or reviewed for distinct reconstruction code; defer only those unexamined components rather than the entire collection.

decisions.title: amigaos-kickstart-source-history
decisions.reason: Surviving original AmigaOS RCS revisions were restored into a browsable Git timeline. This is source-history restoration within the preservation scope; it is not a ROM-derived reconstruction. Version tags and chronology are approximate.

decisions.title: ActionReplayAmiga
decisions.reason: Reverse engineered Action Replay hardware schematics and PAL/FPGA plans; hardware analysis rather than software or firmware reconstruction for the catalogue.

decisions.title: MidiMaze2
decisions.reason: Repository README offers historical shareware archives, disk images and screenshots, without source reconstruction or RE work in the repository.

decisions.title: STOS
decisions.reason: Original and adapted STOS BASIC interpreter/compiler assembly trees qualify as historical Atari ST development tooling. No binary-derived reconstruction or verified modern end-to-end build is claimed; component provenance remains open.

decisions.title: Amberstar original-source archive
decisions.reason: Original incomplete tokenized GFA Assembler development source archive, per its README. Preserve as provenance for Amberstar without treating it as a reverse-engineered reconstruction.

decisions.title: Boulder Dash modern Amiga clone
decisions.reason: New Amiga clone with editor; no primary evidence of recovered code or historical file-format analysis.

decisions.title: Pushover browser port (DOS-derived)
decisions.reason: Static and DOSBox analysis of Pushover DOS executables produced a browser game recreation using DOS data; promoted under DOS origin without asserting Amiga/ST binary or asset analysis.

decisions.title: The Faery Tale Adventure original Amiga sources
decisions.reason: Repository explicitly publishes original Amiga Aztec C/68000 source rather than a reverse-engineered reconstruction. Valuable historical source archive, but outside a distinct RE record.

decisions.title: Exploring Another World — DOS data research
decisions.reason: Concrete Haskell MEMLIST.BIN and BANK parsers qualify as DOS resource analysis. Referencing an Amiga ADF as background does not demonstrate decoding it.

decisions.title: Rockford Patcher — DOS target
decisions.reason: The patcher changes PC Rockford executable and data to recover hidden levels; promoted under DOS only. Historical Amiga art comparisons do not demonstrate Amiga binary patching.

decisions.title: L-Packer — source pending
decisions.reason: Documented and distributed beta packs Amiga and Atari ST executables, qualifying as directly relevant development tooling. Source is promised for a later release and is absent now; source audit and reproducible build are unknown.

decisions.title: Amiga smbfs — upstream protocol reverse engineering
decisions.reason: Amiga SMBFS is a port of Sharity-Light SMB filesystem code. The cited reverse engineering concerns SMB network protocol behavior, while this repository does not analyze a retro Amiga disk, application, executable, or game format; an ordinary native filesystem port alone falls outside the catalogue’s archaeology/tooling scope.

decisions.title: A2232 firmware historical source archive
decisions.reason: Archive contains original Commodore-era sources, including A2232 card firmware, rather than a reconstructed binary or new analysis project.

decisions.title: image-rider STX parser
decisions.reason: The example can extract STX track and sector data and the source implements parser scaffolding. README says formats are not fully parsed; included strictly as exploratory STX tooling.

decisions.title: FujiBoink Amiga conversion
decisions.reason: Atari ST demo to Amiga conversion includes Amiga assembly and asset-generation scripts. Included as a native port, without a binary-derived decompilation claim.

decisions.title: glfrontier FrontierVM 3
decisions.reason: FrontierVM 3 is a later experimental OpenGL renderer in Tom Morton’s existing FrontierVM/Atari ST Frontier lineage, already catalogued as frontier-vm-atari-st. External fe2.s game data and an incomplete renderer limit playability, but neither is a reason to defer a separate discovery decision.

decisions.title: albank1 Agent USA
decisions.reason: The collection lists Agent USA in its README but the tree contains only agentusa.prg, with no Agent USA assembly listing, parser or analysis source to catalogue as an independent reconstruction.

decisions.title: mist64/c64ref
decisions.reason: A curated reference collection and web presentation of ROM listings/memory maps by multiple historical authors. No distinct new binary reconstruction or original parser is established for this repository; the separately buildable c64rom project is catalogued.

decisions.title: Pokefinder-org/final_cartridge_3_original
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this repository as a fork of mist64/final_cartridge, the canonical reconstructed cartridge source added in this batch; no separately evidenced original work was identified.

decisions.title: unorig/DrWhoandtheMinesofTerror
decisions.reason: Repository currently contains only a Markdown item list; the description claims reverse-engineered C64 code, but no source, parser, or reproducible analysis artifact is present.

decisions.title: Piddewitt/C64-Game-Source-Code
decisions.reason: This repository is an index README linking the author’s separate game repositories, with no game source tree of its own; the linked original game studies are already catalogued individually.

decisions.title: g0me3/fceux
decisions.reason: This is a fork of TASEmulators/fceux described only as an Oregon Trail emulator. The current repository description does not establish whether it contains a distinct debugging, analysis or preservation contribution; compare the fork diff and locate project-specific documentation before deciding whether it warrants an independent record.

decisions.title: Crossroads II — old hyphz link
decisions.reason: The January 2025 article cites this old GitHub path; GitHub resolves the repository to MarkRdgOx/crossroads-2-disassembly, already tracked as crossroads2-c64-markrdgox.

decisions.title: Populous C/SDL2 fork
decisions.reason: Fork adds partial C translation but couples it to a game-specific SDL2 Amiga hardware layer, and many game routines remain stubs. Execution boundaries and distinct usable output need an audit before any promotion under the current game-specific-emulation exclusion.

decisions.title: AMSDOS ROM listing in Amstrad-ROM-Sources
decisions.reason: The directory README says the author's own initial work was abandoned and the completed disassembly is an unidentified predecessor's work copied for discoverability; no distinct analysis by this repository is demonstrated for AMSDOS.

decisions.title: GuillianSeed/MetalGear
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes a fully annotated MSX2 disassembly and reproducible Japanese/English ROM builds with expected CRC32 values.

decisions.title: mcolom/arkanoid_msx_disasm
decisions.reason: The annotated source documents z80dasm provenance, a z80asm rebuild command and the expected rebuilt-ROM SHA-1.

decisions.title: ValleyBell/PC98VNResearch
decisions.reason: The collection provides original PC-98 engine/game format research, tools, IDA material and rendered 16-bit x86 disassemblies rather than only links or binary assets.

decisions.title: FuzionCD/lime-juice
decisions.reason: Current C++ compiler/decompiler and image round-trip suite provides substantive PC-98 bytecode/data archaeology tooling with explicit supported and unsupported boundaries.

decisions.title: tomyun/juice
decisions.reason: lime-juice explicitly identifies this Racket implementation as its predecessor and carries the same Juice MES-tool lineage forward; it is retained as relationship evidence rather than a second catalogue record.

decisions.title: nmlgc/ReC98
decisions.reason: Primary documentation describes a maintained source reconstruction of Touhou 1–5 whose rebuilt PC-98 executables remain bit-perfect on every commit.

decisions.title: nmlgc/np2debug
decisions.reason: This Neko Project II fork documents a substantial debugger feature set built specifically for modification and translation of PC-98 binaries.

decisions.title: sidneycadot/Atari8bit_OSB-NTSC-ROM
decisions.reason: This is a substantive OCR/proofreading source-restoration and verified ca65 ROM-reconstruction workflow, not an ordinary original-source mirror.

decisions.title: fa8ntomas/blck-game-engine
decisions.reason: Although the README is only a title, the repository's primary engine.asm is a substantial project-specific annotated 6502 disassembly of Bruce Lee and Atari hardware behavior; unknown build/provenance facts remain explicitly unknown.

decisions.title: milnak/atari-vcs-disassembly
decisions.reason: The root is an aggregate of game sources and submodules, including credited third-party work, rather than one independently authored reconstruction. Individual canonical components require separate deduplication and review.

decisions.title: Dalekamistoso/MSXDUMPTOOLS
decisions.reason: The repository is a redistribution bundle of separately authored MSX utilities and assigns rights to their respective owners; it is useful as a discovery node but not a distinct development project.

decisions.title: radareorg/radare2
decisions.reason: General-purpose multi-platform reversing framework; the README gives no distinct legacy-platform project or extension to track here.

decisions.title: fcambus/jsemu
decisions.reason: Curated index of JavaScript emulators; useful for targeted discovery, but not an authored emulator itself.

decisions.title: VelocityRa/awesome-game-file-format-reversing
decisions.reason: Large curated game-format/resource index; useful as a source, not a standalone analysis tool.

decisions.title: alfishe/amiga-bootcamp
decisions.reason: Amiga development and internals reference, rather than an implemented retro software or analysis tool.

decisions.title: sf2000-qpsx-playstation-emulator
decisions.reason: Consumer PlayStation emulation port for SF2000/GB300; no project-specific recovery or source-debugging function established.

decisions.title: alphaSeclab/awesome-reverse-engineering
decisions.reason: Broad security/reverse-engineering link compilation dominated by modern platforms, not a distinct retro-development project.

decisions.title: danluu/debugging-stories
decisions.reason: General debugging-story link index; its incidental C64 link is not an authored retro software project.

decisions.title: Two9A/c64clicker
decisions.reason: Original browser-based incremental game with a C64 emulator, without documented legacy-software reconstruction or a reusable retro-development tool.

decisions.title: pong-wars
decisions.reason: Small original binary-only visual simulation inspired by a modern web toy; no original-software archaeology or substantial conversion established.

decisions.title: ZX-spectrum-512K-cartridge-Droy-
decisions.reason: Instructions for running an older third-party Windows cartridge creator in a VM; no authored cartridge/tool reconstruction in this repository.

decisions.title: Bread80/Amstrad-CPC-Kicad-Symbols
decisions.reason: KiCad hardware pinout symbols for CPC ICs; no software analysis or developer tool is implemented here.

decisions.title: oldschoolengine2
decisions.reason: Game-specific C64 compatibility engine for recent Covert Bitops titles; assess its execution path and relationship to the games before a catalogue record.

decisions.title: oldschoolengine2-emscripten
decisions.reason: Web/C++ port of the same game-specific engine; assess alongside the Unity implementation rather than counting as a separate game reconstruction.

decisions.title: amigavision/TopazDouble
decisions.reason: Hand-redrawn Amiga font assets; the README expressly says the font file format was not reverse engineered.

decisions.title: jbilander/SimpleDevice
decisions.reason: Amiga device-driver example/template with optional generated objdump output; no legacy-software recovery or standalone analysis tool.

decisions.title: na103/ar3
decisions.reason: Action Replay III hardware schematic reproduction, GAL programming files and ROM binaries; no published debugger source reconstruction.

decisions.title: pararaum/amigaexamples
decisions.reason: Amiga assembly tutorials and a mixed link list; useful for discovering upstream tools and analyses, not a single recovery project.

decisions.title: schlae/amiga-hddlw
decisions.reason: Reverse-engineered third-party Amiga HD floppy-drive adapter hardware and PAL logic; no floppy software or media-analysis tool.

decisions.title: AmstradGameDevChallenge/rpg-adventure
decisions.reason: Original CPC BASIC/C homebrew game and sprite-design examples; cited BASIC disassembly is a third-party reference, not project-specific archaeology.

decisions.title: muckypaws/AmstradCPC
decisions.reason: Mixed archive of period CPC sources, tools and commercial work; components need individual attribution and scope before promotion.

decisions.title: Amiga-68K-BobrHopper
decisions.reason: Port of the author’s new game to AmigaOS using offline sprite baking; no historical-game binary research or reusable analysis tool.

decisions.title: openttd_amiga_68k
decisions.reason: Native port of available OpenTTD 1.0.5 source to AmigaOS with substantial new platform drivers; no recovery of historical binaries established.

decisions.title: Couch-To-64k---Breadboard-Z80-Computer
decisions.reason: Original Z80 breadboard computer tutorial and schematics; no legacy-software reconstruction or separate analysis tool.

decisions.title: CPC_Keyboards
decisions.reason: Replacement CPC keyboard PCB designs and matrix wiring; hardware only.

decisions.title: CPC_ZERO
decisions.reason: Hypothetical new 6502 CPC-like computer based on inspiration from a prototype PCB, not a reconstruction of its software.

decisions.title: CPCModular
decisions.reason: CPC-compatible modular hardware and small test ROM/assembly snippets; no separately implemented CPC software archaeology project.

decisions.title: GreenHAL
decisions.reason: Untested HAL/PAL replacement hardware design and behavior tests; no developer software or recovered firmware.

decisions.title: Soft968-Amstrad-Firmware-Manual
decisions.reason: Hyperlinked CPC firmware manual, useful to verify firmware/jumpblock semantics but not an implemented analysis tool.

decisions.title: z80-character-lcd
decisions.reason: Original Z80 LCD circuit and test code; hardware tutorial outside legacy software/tooling scope.

decisions.title: cadaver.github.io
decisions.reason: Author website and downloadable C64 tool/game archive; useful as a provenance source, not an independent single software project.

decisions.title: hessian
decisions.reason: Original C64 game source; retain to audit the specific games actually run by OldschoolEngine 2, not a binary reconstruction.

decisions.title: mw4
decisions.reason: Original Metal Warrior 4 C64 game source, useful context for the author’s game-specific emulator lineage.

decisions.title: steelranger-demo
decisions.reason: Original source of the C64 Steel Ranger demo; useful for the OldschoolEngine 2 audit, not itself reverse engineering.

decisions.title: CHIP-8-releases
decisions.reason: Acorn Electron binary-only consumer CHIP-8 emulator without documented developer debugger, analysis or source recovery capabilities.

decisions.title: ckwin
decisions.reason: Historical Windows/OS/2 Kermit terminal and file-transfer application source; this candidate documents an application continuation without a specific recovery or retro development tool contribution.

decisions.title: seqbox
decisions.reason: General file-system-independent archive/recovery container; no historical computer software or platform-specific analysis in the project scope.

decisions.title: hid2ami
decisions.reason: HID to Amiga/Atari input adapter hardware and firmware; no independent historical-software recovery or developer-analysis tool evidenced.

decisions.title: z80-open-silicon
decisions.reason: Open silicon pin-compatible Z80 CPU replacement with tapeout and PCB validation; hardware recreation outside the software catalogue.

decisions.title: electrobots-going-underground-releases
decisions.reason: Original modern Electron/BBC game distributed as tape/disk and executable images; no source-recovery or development-tool output in this release repository.

decisions.title: electrobots-releases
decisions.reason: Original modern Electron/BBC game distributed as tape/disk and executable images; no source-recovery or development-tool output in this release repository.

decisions.title: elementum-releases
decisions.reason: Original modern Electron/BBC game release images and instructions, without a demonstrated software archaeology or tooling component.

decisions.title: flappy-bird-releases
decisions.reason: Electron/BBC adaptation distributed as playable tape/disk images only; no distinct analysed-source or developer-tool artifact.

decisions.title: lode-runner-2021-releases
decisions.reason: Electron Lode Runner game release images and play/edit instructions; no evidenced recovered source or development tooling here.

decisions.title: manic-miner-2021-releases

decisions.title: s-macke/SAM

decisions.title: Babaliba for Atari ST
decisions.reason: Authored Atari ST conversion of Dinamic Babaliba. README describes observing the Spectrum game and recreating graphics pixel by pixel, retaining map/mechanics and adding saves, pause and POKEs. C game, asset conversion scripts and TOS releases are published; no binary-derived reconstruction claim.

decisions.title: Doom8088: Motorola 68000 Edition
decisions.reason: Source-derived native Doom port for low-memory 68000-family computers, based on FrenkelS/Doom8088. README documents Episode 1 only, reduced rendering and no music/saves/multiplayer; Atari ST backend and build script are published. This is a native source port, not reverse engineering.

decisions.title: m68k-atari-dev
decisions.reason: Cross-compilation and remote-debug development system using GCC/newlib/binutils, a purpose-written TOS GDB server and ELF-to-PRG conversion that preserves symbol addresses. Source inventory includes packet/protocol, exception/context handling and converter implementation. The Windows build is documented as problematic; no host or hardware operation was independently reproduced.

decisions.title: HAS (High Assembler)
decisions.reason: Python compiler for an assembly-first high-level language with typed control flow, inline assembly, macros, register control and Amiga libraries. hasc contains parser, AST, validators, code generator and optimizer; asset tools and examples remain part of this coherent compiler project. The compiler emits assembly and requires separately installed vasm/vlink for executables.

decisions.title: Amiga ASM Development Workflow
decisions.reason: Linux automation pipeline for Amiga assembly projects: GIMP/PNG/IFF conversion, ZX0 packing, copper palette/icon generation, assembly/linking and bootable ADF construction. Includes a credited demonstration derived from Bare-Metal Amiga Programming and Salvador decompression; catalogue scope is the integrated development tooling, not a new disassembly.

decisions.title: Retrodev
decisions.reason: Integrated CPC development environment with bitmap/tile/sprite/map conversion, palette solving, RASM builds, scriptable exports and timing-validated Z80 raster-handler generation. README marks CPC/CPC+ supported while Spectrum, C64 and MSX are only prepared for; do not advertise those planned targets as implemented.

decisions.title: Slotshot
decisions.reason: Original C64 puzzle shooter with substantial published PyCo game source, graphics/music includes and build configuration. README states its PyCo compiler remains private and generated assembly/PRG/D64 outputs are not in this repository; public reproducible compilation is therefore unverified, despite documented play controls and runtime instructions.

decisions.title: Outrun 2026
decisions.reason: Released CPC 6128 fan conversion based on Master System OutRun. Michel Louvet states Claude Code wrote a native Z80 engine and extraction/music tools, with measured tracks, scenery and handling and SN76489-to-AY music conversion. Author reports emulator and real-hardware testing. Inspected Outrun V0.8.zip contains only Outrun V0.8.dsk (194816 bytes); no source or patches were linked, so source availability/compilability and detailed architecture remain unverified. Claims of native rewriting and AI model identity are attributed to the author, not independently reproduced. Targeted public search checked the project and itch creator/profile links, Outrun/CPC/title and Michel Louvet/GitHub searches. No matching public source was found; the similarly named yonifra/outrun2026 repository is an unrelated HTML5 game.

decisions.title: FreeMiNT
decisions.reason: Primary README and kernel/documentation inventory establish ongoing community maintenance of the existing open-source MiNT system. Keep as a reference/source node, rather than a new reconstruction or substantial newly authored port under the source-map rule that routine open-source maintenance alone is not an independent catalogue addition.

decisions.title: Korg DW6000 editor
decisions.reason: Primary README and src/DW6000.ino establish a Teensy-based hardware MIDI/SysEx editor. The CPC mention is autobiographical background, not published CPC software or recovery of the historical editor. Outside this legacy-computer development pass.

decisions.title: ByteBox — Amstrad CPC emulator and monitor
decisions.reason: The cached upstream page documents a Rust CPC 6128 emulator with Z80 stepping, disassembly, breakpoints, watchpoints and traces. Current repository metadata and raw README fetches both return 404. Recheck the repository's public availability or locate its current canonical URL and inspect the core before promoting.

decisions.title: Retrobrews C64 games collection
decisions.reason: Repository is a third-party binary distribution collection: D64/PRG/TAP images, screenshots, descriptions and a game-list XML. It provides no source, disassembly, analysis or independent development tooling, so it is a discovery source rather than a standalone project.

decisions.title: c64 — C64 Ultimate command-line and disk tools
decisions.reason: Concrete TypeScript CLI provides C64 Ultimate program/media deployment, scripted machine control, PETSCII keyboard input, and implemented D64 directory parsing/creation/renaming. These are directly relevant retro-development and disk-image tools at coherent repository scope.

decisions.title: AmstradCPC6128 — ZX-Uno/ZX-Tres FPGA core
decisions.reason: Synthesizable CPC system implementation extends Miguel Angel Rodriguez Jodar's CPC464 design with 128 KB banking and SD-backed two-drive disk emulation. The repository includes machine integration RTL, Z80 core, disk-controller logic, project files and known-good board releases; this is a general CPC implementation, not game-specific emulation.

decisions.title: C64 — cycle-accurate C64/1541 emulator and debugger
decisions.reason: Substantive C11 implementation of the C64 and 1541 as separate cycle-stepped machines, with disk handling, peripheral models, tests, snapshots and bus watchpoints. Documentation and source establish a general emulator useful for debugging historical software.

decisions.title: Robot Jet Action — original C64 game source
decisions.reason: Author-published original C64 arcade game sources include substantial KickC game logic, level data, native assembly support and a documented build. Qualifies as concrete homebrew/native development under the current scope; no reverse-engineering provenance is claimed.

decisions.title: Return Home — Amstrad CPC Z80 space shooter
decisions.reason: Substantial original Z80 game source, RASM build pipeline and ready-to-run CPC disk image demonstrate concrete native homebrew. The custom Z80 emulator/profiler is supporting testing infrastructure; the promoted output is a native CPC game.

decisions.title: c64 — native C64 scrolling game experiments
decisions.reason: Original C64 game implementation contains substantial native assembly, generated tile/sprite assets, a build/run script, and dated PRG snapshots. The author documents gameplay controls, completed tagged playthroughs and concrete raster/renderer optimization work.

decisions.title: Hägar the Horrible — C64 original-source preservation
decisions.reason: Archive preserves programmer-supplied original game sources and disk artifacts and makes the tokenized Turbo Assembler source readable through documented extraction. This is source preservation under the broadened scope, not binary-derived reconstruction or a new disassembly.

decisions.title: Brick Blaster — Amstrad CPC arcade game
decisions.reason: Substantive native CPC C/inline-Z80 game code, localized disk/tape builds and assets establish original homebrew. The RVM web portal runs the native CPC output; it is ancillary and does not turn the repository into a game-specific-emulation-only project.

decisions.title: Citadel — original Amiga source archive
decisions.reason: Original 1995 Citadel game source, data and editor archive, with substantive 68000 game-engine code and documented AsmOne build/run steps. Qualifies as original-source preservation under the broadened retro-development scope; it is not a binary-derived reconstruction.

decisions.title: ACE — Amiga C game engine and asset tools
decisions.reason: Concrete C hardware-support/game framework for classic Amiga, including blitter/copper/input implementations, example showcase and asset-conversion tooling. This is original native retro-development infrastructure, not a game-specific emulator.

decisions.title: Amiga Assembly Library — original source and C bindings
decisions.reason: Substantive original 1990s Amiga assembly.library code is present in public/download/asm, including the library resident/function table and implementations, plus C interfaces and examples. The enclosing modern documentation site and archive form one project.

decisions.title: Menace — Amiga Format source restoration and asset tools
decisions.reason: Restores and modernizes Menace code published across Amiga Format coverdisks, with assembled-game documentation and substantive updated source. Includes a C# decoder for the game's graphics data; this is more than a passive magazine mirror.

decisions.title: ACE BASIC — enhanced native Amiga compiler
decisions.reason: Active continuation of the historical ACE BASIC compiler with real K&R C parser/code-generator source, 68k runtime libraries, modern VBCC build migration and test tooling. The native compiler and IDE support form a single coherent development project.

decisions.title: HelloAmi — Amiga bootblocks and Workbench library reimplementation
decisions.reason: Despite the Hello World title, the repository implements a replacement icon.library for booting ROM Workbench, a dynamic version.library, OFS image/bootblock tools and compatibility research. These are concrete system reimplementation and retro-development artifacts.

decisions.title: ANA — Amiga C game framework and development tools
decisions.reason: Early-stage native Amiga C framework with actual runtime/rendering/input/sound implementations, game showcases, asset conversion and a distributed VS Code extension. Repository-wide scope covers the framework and its companion tools.

decisions.title: ST Sopwith — native Atari ST port
decisions.reason: Distinct native Atari ST C/assembly port descended from released Sopwith/SDL Sopwith source, with a real Atari framebuffer/blitter backend and downloadable .TOS/.ST releases. Upstream fork status does not make it a passive duplicate.

decisions.title: Perihelion Atari ST assembly tutorial republication
decisions.reason: Primarily republishes perihelion's existing Atari ST tutorials as AsciiDoc and separates/reformats their assembly examples, with only minor edits. Its short Makefile orchestrates existing vasm, zip2st and Hatari. Reviewed source establishes an educational reference rather than a distinct recovered program or independently implemented development/recovery tool, so retain a source/decision but no separate project.

decisions.title: UNO — native card game across vintage computers
decisions.reason: One original homebrew card game with shared C game rules and platform-specific native backends across vintage machines, including concrete Amiga and Atari ST implementations and upstream gameplay verification. Track the coherent whole repository rather than splitting each port.

decisions.title: DICE-nx — restored Amiga C compiler toolchain
decisions.reason: Substantial restoration and continued development of the original DICE compiler suite, with an implemented 68k code generator, native assembly helpers, assembler, linker and runtime source. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation and directly relevant native toolchain work.

decisions.title: Parcade — native Amiga demo source
decisions.reason: Creator-published, substantial native 68000 Amiga intro implementation with multiple effects, hardware takeover/restore, music integration and assembly instructions. Track the complete intro rather than separate effect files.

decisions.title: Attack of the PETSCII Robots — native Amiga translation
decisions.reason: Substantial native fan conversion with first-person development notes, translated C++ game logic and Amiga-specific assembly/rendering. Source translation, not embedded guest-CPU emulation.

decisions.title: Phantom Fighter — Amiga source archive and modern recreation
decisions.reason: Creator-published recovery of substantial original 1988 Amiga game code plus concrete source-based native Python/JavaScript recreations. The modern paths implement game logic directly and do not use game-specific CPU pseudo-emulation.

decisions.title: Devil's Temple — native Amiga game source
decisions.reason: Substantial creator-attributed native Amiga homebrew/spin-off implementation, corroborated by the creator's released-game page. Actual game source extends far beyond a copied loader/template.

decisions.title: Alpha Waves — original Atari ST source archive
decisions.reason: Substantive original Atari ST game source and assets, with author/date headers and concrete 68k game/polygon implementation. Historical preservation qualifies independently of unknown buildability; not labelled a binary-derived disassembly.

decisions.title: Hard Drivin' — archival source and incomplete Linux restoration
decisions.reason: Concrete historical game-source restoration with substantial game logic and modified C build scaffolding. Actual x86/DOS code overrides the misleading ST repository label. Missing runtime stubs limit completeness but do not negate the existing archival/restoration work.

decisions.title: Alice Personal Pascal — historical IDE source and portability work
decisions.reason: Substantial period programming environment with preserved Atari ST/Unix source, interpreter, editor, debugger and actual portability scaffolding. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation, not a tutorial or unrelated modern application.

decisions.title: StingRay GamePatches — Amiga compatibility fixes and trainers
decisions.reason: Concrete binary-derived patch implementations, identified game offsets and documented compatibility defects. A small README is unnecessary: source comments and substantive assembly establish the work. Track the coherent patch collection at repository scope.

decisions.title: FujiBoink — original ST source archive
decisions.reason: Preserves the original 1986 FujiBoink C/68000 demo source and period documentation. The already tracked mnemo70/fujiboink conversion repository retains the same six historical ST source components under st_source, with matching creator/date headers and implementation. Retain this useful original-source reference linked to that lineage, without adding a second overlapping source-only project. All six historical C/assembly components match after whitespace normalization; five match with CRLF normalization alone.

decisions.title: Ghost Town — C16 disassembly and native Commodore ports
decisions.reason: Substantial annotated Ghost Town recovery includes original-platform logic, bug fixes, languages, graphics, SID music and native C64/C128 conversion. The two ports and supporting tools are one coherent repository-wide project.

decisions.title: C64 crack-intro disassemblies — Tomaszndt
decisions.reason: Five source listings contain concrete C64 intro disassembly with origin links, labels and analysis of raster interrupts, scrolling, system calls and music. Lack of a README/build script does not negate the existing research; catalogue at whole-repository scope.

decisions.title: Music-player disassemblies — C64 and Atari 8-bit
decisions.reason: Concrete labelled disassembly and sequencer/pattern analysis of C64 International Karate SID and multiple Atari POKEY players, accompanied by Frida projects and source music files. This is subsystem research rather than full-game reconstruction and is kept as one coherent archive.

decisions.title: c64-ruby — C64 assets, code generation and build tools
decisions.reason: Implemented Ruby library provides VIC-II image conversion, 6502 assembly/byte generation, PRG merging, VICE snapshot injection and ca65/ld65/Exomizer build automation. It is directly relevant development tooling beyond its short library overview.

decisions.title: Bitmapper — C64 multicolor bitmap converter
decisions.reason: Concrete Java/Swing cross-development tool converts images to C64 multicolor data and exports Koala files, with palette selection, per-cell color constraints, dithering and a GUI. The nested NetBeans project is the repository's single tool.

decisions.title: oscar64nvim — C64 build and debug integration
decisions.reason: Working implementation exists for project-aware Oscar64 compile commands, asynchronous process handling, Quickfix compiler diagnostics, assembly viewing and VICE/RetroDebugger launch. This is a distinct Neovim integration, not an independent compiler/emulator.

decisions.title: Mutant Monty — native Amiga Scorpion conversion
decisions.reason: Creator-published Scorpion source contains substantial Mutant Monty game logic, actors, 41 level maps, graphics and sound, with released Amiga ADF/WHDLoad builds linked from the creator page. It qualifies as a native fan conversion; original C64/CPC binary analysis is not claimed.

decisions.title: Mars Patrol — creator-restored C64 Moon Patrol conversion
decisions.reason: Creator documents recovery of his unfinished 1985 C64 Moon Patrol conversion by disassembling and reassembling the old binary in 2024, then implementing substantial missing gameplay. Published PRG/D64 outputs and explicit PAL VICE play testing support a concrete restoration even though recovered source files are not published.

decisions.title: Lawn Job — author-restored C64 BASIC source
decisions.reason: Michael Buhidar republishes and verifies his own 1983/84 C64 BASIC game from the October 1984 Ahoy! type-in. Complete game listing and tokenized PRG are present, with original-author provenance, line-check verification and explicit VICE operation.

decisions.title: c64_disassembly_reader — derivative hex-listing converter
decisions.reason: README identifies this as a converter of mist64/c64disasm's existing hex-assembly text into BASIC/KERNAL binary images. c64_read_dis.erl parses listed addresses/bytes, fills address gaps and writes bytes; it adds no independent disassembly, recovery analysis or substantive compiler. Excluded under the workflow's rule for merely converting somebody else's analysis; original listing attribution is preserved.

decisions.title: Knight Lore CPC reconstruction
decisions.reason: RAM-derived CPC Knight Lore reconstruction contains symbolic Z80 assembly, data extraction and detailed engine analysis, with original and experimental rendering branches. Primary main-branch documentation reports successful RASM assembly and standalone snapshot boot to the real menu. This does not establish full playability or complete byte matching; the browser component is described only as a room visualizer.

decisions.title: Fruity Frank Kotlin
decisions.reason: Substantive Kotlin/LibGDX recreation of Fruity Frank with game-state, enemies, collision, scoring and desktop/Android launchers. It recreates CPC gameplay rather than documenting binary-derived reconstruction. Gradle pins old Kotlin/Android dependencies; no independent build or run was performed.

decisions.title: Phantomas 2.0 CPC
decisions.reason: Author-published 2018 CPC remake of the Dinamic game, with substantial native assembly, room data, audio and public English/Spanish CDT plus DSK releases. No binary-derived reconstruction or byte-equivalence claim is made.

decisions.title: Airwolf2023
decisions.reason: Original C#/MonoGame re-creation of the CPC Airwolf gameplay with real level, enemy, helicopter, collision and UI code. Creator explicitly says it is not emulation, recreates only gameplay and may omit original features. This is a modern remake, not a native CPC port or a claimed disassembly.

decisions.title: CPCtelera
decisions.reason: Substantive CPC C/assembly development framework, low-level hardware library, asset tools and reproducible-project build infrastructure. Inspected keyboard implementation directly programs the PPI/PSG; examples and content tools form the same coherent repository.

decisions.title: RASM
decisions.reason: Author-maintained C Z80 cross-assembler includes CPC cartridge/snapshot/disk/tape generation, integrated compression, patching support and debug symbols. Inspected actual assembler source, integrated API example and build files. Z80 is the output instruction set, not a claim that the host executable runs on Z80.

decisions.title: DAMS
decisions.reason: Original author preserved and annotated the commercial 1985 CPC DAMS source, with a tokenized-source encoder/decoder and documented self-hosting rebuild procedure. Actual dams.dams assembly and C++ conversion tool establish substantive source restoration, not a binary-only distribution.

decisions.title: HyperLoader
decisions.reason: Concrete fast CPC tape loader with adaptive pulse measurement, synchronization and native loading code, paired with a Python CDT generator. Source credits Mert Boru's TurboLoader as the basis; this repository adds an implemented paired workflow rather than a passive binary mirror.

decisions.title: Amstrad Diagnostics
decisions.reason: Author-maintained native diagnostic suite tests RAM, ROM, keyboard and CRTC behavior, with substantial hardware routines and distinct ROM, RAM, cartridge, disk and tape build variants. Companion ROM dump code supports retro system investigation.

decisions.title: Ninja Carnage
decisions.reason: Creator-published multi-platform native adventure game source, with substantial CPC/C64 C game code and Amiga assembly implementation plus asset/build tools. Track the common game once at repository scope; referenced Spectrum/ST ports are not claimed as present in this repository.

decisions.title: Manic Miner: Retro!
decisions.reason: Primary README and source establish a distinct playable Z80-disassembly-derived C++ port with explicit remaining limitations.

decisions.title: iDSK

decisions.title: FROGMAN — BBC Micro game disassembly and remaster
decisions.reason: Fully annotated BeebASM reconstruction of Matt Godbolt and Richard Talbot-Watkins's 1993 BBC platformer, obtained by dumping emulator memory after its timing-dependent 55-stage encryption loader. Upstream reports byte-exact original engine/game-code matches and playable remastered output for BBC Master/Model B. The verification scope is code regions, not an asserted byte-identical whole remastered disc. Credits explicitly name Claude.

decisions.title: The Shaft — Amstrad CPC 6128 homebrew platformer
decisions.reason: Original CPC 6128 Z80 platformer with fifty-nine levels, banked level data, compiled sprites, combat and seven mini-games. The miniature Z80 test runner is development tooling, not the game execution path.

decisions.title: Desolate — TI-83 Plus to ZX Spectrum native port

The build assembles with Pasmo/SjASMPlus, compresses with LZSA and produces TAP/TZX. README links walkthroughs and related Vector-06c/UKNC ports.

decisions.title: Fred in Space — ZX Spectrum Next homebrew game

decisions.title: Chip's Challenge — Atari Lynx native-C static recompilation
decisions.reason: Experimental native-C static recompilation of the Atari Lynx game using lynxrecomp. The game-specific host registers generated functions and calls the translated entry point; it does not execute guest instructions through a CPU interpreter. Upstream demonstrates title-screen rendering, while interactive live input remains future work. User-supplied cartridge/boot ROM and generated C are required. Only fixed-function Suzy/Mikey support hardware is modeled by the runtime.

Build and playability are supported by upstream clean-rebuild and emulator regression reports, not a local independent build. v1.7 reports 183 regression commands plus sprite fixtures passing; physical EverDrive/NTSC validation remains pending. decisions.title: Side Arms MD — native Mega Drive arcade port

Requires 27 hash-checked files from the user's MAME sidearms World set; no ROM data or compiled cartridge is distributed in the repository. Upstream reports complete section/ending QA and v1.2 software regression passes. Physical MiSTer and flash-cart confirmation remains outstanding, and heavy scenes still drop frames. Current release notes describe local builds rather than a GitHub release or a confirmed itch upload.

decisions.title: volamos — AmigaOS CLI compatibility runtime
decisions.reason: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof.
