decisions.title: Burger Time — native C64 arcade port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native C64 reimplementation/port of the arcade BurgerTime game, with substantive burger-layer falling, collision, landing and completion logic. The inspected evidence does not establish a recovered arcade disassembly. Gameplay source, graphics/SID resources and binary/build artifacts are present, but no complete modern build was reproduced. KickAssembler and Exomizer-related packaging requirements remain source-inspected; all build flags remain null. Nick Sherman/1888games supplies a separate native C64 implementation of BurgerTime. Existing jotd-burgertime-amiga is a different Amiga arcade transcode, not the same repository or output. Original arcade title, graphics and music rights remain separate; no blanket repository license was found.

decisions.title: Caveman — electronic tabletop game C64 port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native C64 remake of the Grandstand/Tomy/Tandy electronic tabletop Caveman game, with movement positions, egg carrying, sprite handling and frame code. The unreviewed VIC-20 subfolder does not establish another supported port. README names KickAssembler, CharPad, SpritePad, GoatTracker and Exomizer; native gameplay modules and assets are supplied. No build command, clean compilation or gameplay test was independently executed, so all build flags remain null. Nick Sherman is credited for code and graphics; Richard Bayliss, Stepz and Mike Richmond have separate music/SFX credits. README permission for an attributed CSDB upload is narrower than a general code/asset license. Exact original tabletop hardware remains unresolved.

decisions.title: Sniper — native C64 homebrew source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Source-backed original C64 homebrew game with title, gameplay, game-over/explosion states, joystick handling, score and health. Binary assets and native PRGs accompany actual implementation; completion is unverified. No README or license file exists in the inspected recursive tree. a.asm and graphics/audio/PRG assets establish substantive source, but the assembler/version, clean build, execution and final release status remain unverified; all build flags remain null. Repository metadata identifies the author’s C64 Sniper homebrew. No older commercial subject or upstream source fork was established; no broad code/audio/graphics license should be inferred from publication.

decisions.title: Word Writer 6 — original and ACME-converted C64 source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Original Timeworks Word Writer 6 application source, preserving 2500AD assembly and an ACME-converted build tree with editor, printer, dictionary and overlay modules. This is author-source restoration/assembler conversion, not binary decompilation. README supplies ACME/VS Code assembly, VICE launch, c1541 packing and overlay extraction steps. Only the PowerShell overlay extractor is explicitly described as tested on Windows 10. These do not establish a reproduced assembler build or working application, so all build flags remain null. Jeff Lomax’s original source is transformed using his converttoacme tool and an Esshahn VS Code template. The inspected MIT LICENSE supplies a repository grant; separately supplied tools and asset notices remain distinct.

decisions.title: Kye — native C64 puzzle-game port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native C64 port of Colin Garbutt’s Windows puzzle game Kye. The author explicitly deduced undocumented object interactions by testing the original, supporting a behavioral-RE-derived port rather than a recovered original source claim. README gives KickAssembler 5.24 commands and separate PAL/NTSC release packaging. Those commands and the download link were not independently built or exercised. The 255-active-object limit, differing respawn behavior and missing editor/disk-level loading are explicit; all build flags remain null. Colin Garbutt is credited for the original game; Patai Gergely for the C64 port/music, with individually credited contributed level packs. The GPL-3.0 LICENSE should not erase original design and level-set provenance.

decisions.title: Interword — recovered original C64 source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Recovered original 1992 commissioned C64 port of the Amiga Interword word processor. An attic floppy backup preserved the source; upstream warns it is probably not the final product version. This is original-source recovery, not a new reverse-engineered port. The recovered source uses historical assembler/Turbo Assembler-oriented material and separate libraries linked through jump tables. README links a VICE assembly guide, but it was not exercised. The backup may predate the final release, so all build and byte-identity flags remain null. Interactivision commissioned the C64 adaptation from its Amiga version; recovered source is credited to the original programmer, with disk conversion/retrieval acknowledgements. Original packaging, manuals and final disks were lost, and no broad license grant was found.

decisions.title: Tiny Pascal — C64 compiler and runtime port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. C64 port and revival of the Chung/Yuen Tiny Pascal compiler, with BASIC compiler code, p-code generation and an implemented 6510 runtime/translator. The initial no-runtime statement is historical; current README/source establish subsequent runtime work. compiler.bas implements token/symbol tables and p-code generation, while runtime.asm contains implemented stack and I/O routines. process.sh invokes petcat/c1541 through a machine-specific VICE path. No compiler/runtime build or test program was executed, and planned file I/O and richer Pascal types remain incomplete; all build flags remain null. Preserve Chung and Yuen’s 1978 book/compiler provenance and Bill Fahle’s historical C64 port/revival. README says 1985/July 2026 whereas compiler.bas comments say 1984/June 2026, so no exact reconstruction-start date is chosen. MIT repository metadata does not erase historical attribution.

decisions.title: DraCopy and DraBrowse — Commodore file utilities
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native Commodore file/disk copy and browser utilities, continued from Sascha Bader’s released source. The reviewed implementation performs concrete directory, file, disk and optional RAM-expansion operations; this is utility source development, not recovered game code. README explicitly reports successful historical builds on Linux and macOS using GNU make and cc65, so compilable=true is upstream-only. No local build, disk/file operation or runtime test was performed. Release links alone do not prove current behavior; runnable/playable/byte_exact remain null. Doj’s branch descends from Bader’s 1.0c and independently reimplements some 1.0e features; it is not simply the 1.0e branch or the unpublished 1.0d source. The custom permission requires original-source/author attribution and includes no warranty; no SPDX label is guessed.

decisions.title: Open Curse of Sherwood — C64 game remake
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native C#/Raylib-cs work-in-progress remake of Mastertronic’s C64 The Curse of Sherwood, with player movement, shooting, death/respawn and score implementation. It is not a guest CPU wrapper or recovered original assembly. The csproj targets net9.0 and Raylib-cs 7.0.1, and README supplies source/release Windows launch instructions. No build or game execution was performed; release existence does not establish completion, and all build flags remain null. The project explicitly remakes Mastertronic’s game. GPL-3.0 repository metadata does not itself clear the original game graphics/title or bundled third-party font; original and dependency rights remain distinct.

decisions.title: C64 Studio / RetroDevStudio — C64 development IDE
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. C64 Studio/RetroDevStudio is a Windows Forms retro-development IDE with implemented ASM/BASIC parsers, media/graphics editors, build configurations and external-emulator debugging. Linux support is through Wine/PlayOnLinux, not a native Linux GUI build. README reports success under PlayOnLinux/Ubuntu and testing under Linux Mint 21.3 with Wine, so runnable=true is an upstream-only compatibility-layer claim. Current csproj frameworks are net10.0-windows, net3.5 and net4.8; the README’s older .NET 6 binary list is not substituted for current project configuration. No compilation was performed. C64Studio repository and RetroDevStudio source namespace identify one continuing IDE project, not separate roots. Inspected license.md grants MIT for C64 Studio and lists separately licensed dependencies including LGPL-3.0; GitHub NOASSERTION does not replace the actual notices.

decisions.title: SMB1 transpiler — Apple II/C64 VERA port rebuilder
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. C99 ROM-to-disk rebuilder for an existing Apple II A2VERA/C64 VERA Super Mario Bros. port, combining positional game-code transformations, Super Mario All-Stars graphics conversion and embedded 6502 glue. It is not a general compiler, a stock-machine port or an original-source archive. README explicitly reports building and running both MinGW-w64 x86_64 and i686 builder executables, plus generated C64-image boot to the title screen. Compilable/runnable=true are upstream-only and scoped to those reports; full playability remains unknown. No candidate build, ROM processing, hardware test or byte comparison occurred. Disk/file checksum claims are not independent byte-exact evidence. This wrapper rebuilds the a2vera port using generated a2vera_blobs.h; the assembler/source pipeline lives elsewhere. Adrian Black’s controller code is MIT, Krill Loader v166 is BSD-3-Clause, and Joe Burks’s A2VERA hardware is separately credited. Main code is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, explicitly not OSI open source. Nintendo ROMs/game art/code and generated disk images receive no license grant; upstream says not to redistribute the outputs.

decisions.title: C64 archeology tools — T64 extraction utility
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Focused C64 preservation utility collection whose reviewed substantive component is t64-dump, a Python T64 listing/extraction parser with ZIP input. It is not a general disassembler suite. The actual Python parser supports listing/extraction, with a focused README. No execution, fixture tests or packaging build was performed; script presence alone does not prove a currently functioning utility. All build flags remain null. The repository’s preservation-tool identity is retained at one root even though the reviewed implementation is a t64-dump subfolder. GPL-3.0 repository metadata governs the tool scope; user-supplied archive contents have their own rights.

decisions.title: Food Truck — C64 game source and prototypes
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Original C64 Food Truck source and prototypes with customer-arrival, queue and sales-state implementation. One root contains multiple experiments/backups; it is not a confirmed finished commercial-game reconstruction. FoodTruck.cbmprj names foodtruck.prg and lists multiple assembly files, while sellcycle.asm implements a sales prototype. README is title-only; exact current IDE/assembler prerequisites, coherent final build and gameplay completion remain unverified. All build flags remain null. TheRealZerfall identifies Food Truck as the author’s C64 game. Multiple prototype files stay within one project record; no historical precursor, independent fork or code/asset license grant was established.

decisions.title: Reblitz64 — reconstructed Blitz! BASIC compiler
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Structured-source reconstruction and JavaScript port of the Blitz!/Austro-Speed C64 BASIC V2 compiler. Original BASIC control flow was rewritten and transpiled, with assembly helpers replaced in JavaScript; the main output does not execute a guest 6502 interpreter. README links a live browser compiler, documents Node invocation and reports a measured compiler benchmark, so runnable=true is an upstream-only compiler report. Regeneration uses petcat, basictransplr, js-beautify, Perl and shell scripts, none run here. The incomplete regex-dependent transpiler can alter FOR-loop semantics; compilation/output correctness and byte identity remain unverified. Preserve Blitz!/Austro-Speed compiler provenance, the separately compared blitz 0.1 emulator port, the author’s basictransplr helper and CrankThePRINT rendering tool. The helper is not a general semantics-preserving transpiler. No repository-wide license was found.

decisions.title: C64 KERNAL and BASIC — ASM6502 source port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Assembler-source port of preserved Commodore KERNAL V3 and BASIC V2 source from mist64/cbmsrc, with layout/ROM patches and a checksum helper. The contribution is modern assembler adaptation and reproducible-ROM tooling, not independently recovered or binary-decompiled original source. README supplies assembly, split-ROM layout, checksum patching and MD5 verification commands, with flags that change replica behavior. Commands and reference hashes are recipes, not reproduced builds. No ROM was assembled, patched or compared, so all build flags remain null. Explicit predecessor: https://github.com/mist64/cbmsrc, already represented in the discovery-source index as github-mist64-cbmsrc, not an existing project record. Preserve that original-source lineage and the distinct ASM6502 conversion contribution. kernal/disclaim.a65 retains Commodore’s 1983 computer-use restrictions; cbmsum.c separately declares BSD-3. The entire repository must not be called BSD/open source.

decisions.title: rtl8139re.device — AmigaOS 4 driver reconstruction
decisions.reason: Repository describes reverse-engineered C reconstruction of Hyperion rtl8139.device; native SANA-II resident driver implements PCI enumeration, transmit handling and now IRQ/RX infrastructure. Makefile cross-compiles ppc-amigaos-gcc with -mcpu=440; target is AmigaOS 4 on QEMU sam460ex, with real Sam460ex/AmigaOne hardware only expected. Latest history documents Roadshow packet/copy-hook debugging and an RX rollback, so README pending-status table is stale relative to source. Incomplete driver: latest commit rolls back RX-side CallHookPkt dispatch; no claim of working full TCP/IP or production readiness. License explicitly TBD. Real-hardware compatibility is unverified; QEMU reports are upstream-only. PPC build flags identify target ISA, not 68k Amiga compatibility or minimum RAM.

decisions.title: Pinball Illusions — browser reconstruction
decisions.reason: Independent TypeScript browser reconstruction of the 1995 four-disk Amiga AGA release, with N-ball fixed-point simulation, collision maps, table mission-bytecode interpreter, canvas rendering and audio. Inspected ball-physics.ts and package.json show real implementation and Node/TypeScript build/test scripts; no 68k runtime wrapper is required. Original AGA release has three tables in this project; PC/console-exclusive Vikings is intentionally excluded. Inspected mode-vm.ts explicitly leaves eight mission opcodes unimplemented and deliberately ends missions when the ball ends, diverging from original behavior. This is not full gameplay parity. Upstream gameplay/parity/test counts are not independently validated and README explicitly retains contact-frame physics and sprite/collision alignment discrepancies. Ships disk-derived artwork, audio, music, geometry and mission data. Build rights gate requires PINBALL_ILLUSIONS_DERIVED_AUTHORIZED=1; this operator assertion is not evidence of redistribution permission. No repository license found. Re-extraction needs operator-owned original disks; clean-room description is upstream wording, not a legal conclusion.

decisions.title: Perihelion 2.0 — Amiga BBX game reconstruction
decisions.reason: Rebuilds Craig Dorrell’s Amiga BBX door game using surviving introduction, screenshots and original bitmap fonts; Python engine serves terminal and browser clients. Actual gameplay module implements movement, combat, economy, fleets and multiplayer state. Amiga-font parser recovers preserved glyphs into modern rendering assets. Historical README.TXT supports Amiga BBX origin; modern README.md carefully distinguishes surviving material from unavailable binary/full manual. No original game binary is available to this project: reconstruction includes inferred rules, naming choices, player recollections and modern additions, so it is not a binary-derived decompilation. No license found; original font/artwork is preserved rather than newly authored. Rights and full behavioral equivalence remain unverified. Repository description says 1988 while modern README specifically reconstructs the 1992 version 2.0; retain 1992 target and do not silently harmonize these dates.

decisions.title: ReFlood — native reconstruction of Amiga Flood
decisions.reason: C99/SDL2 native source reconstruction of Flood with game logic, asset extractor, audio/presentation, editor, deterministic test harness and experimental local split-screen mode. CMake defines a reusable flood_core and reflood/editor targets; src/game.c implements native gameplay rather than invoking an Amiga emulator. Only supported original IPF revision can be converted via disk-analyse and extracted; manifest checks reconstructed files. Original Flood data is not distributed in releases and is required for play and gameplay tests. Needs a legally obtained supported IPF plus disk-analyse with SPS/CAPS support. GPL-3.0 covers repository code; it does not license original assets. Multiplayer is experimental, editor cannot yet create/edit triggers. Latest editor-focus report explicitly lacks an XFCE/SDL runtime check. We did not build or run the game or editor.

decisions.title: Rog — C64 demo disassembly and extraction toolkit
decisions.reason: Preserves a C64 demo via generated/named 6502 assembly and Python graph-disassembly, bitmap/charset/sprite and SID extraction tools. Disassembler implements entry discovery, control-flow traversal, overlap/conflict tracking and I/O-register symbolization; sources are substantive rather than only a binary archive. Committed coverage report shows 2,674 instructions/7,184 decoded bytes out of a 46,911-byte payload (15.31%). Remaining data bytes are emitted to support rebuild; 15.31% coverage is not complete semantic reconstruction. README provides 64tass/cmp byte-rebuild instructions but does not establish our own successful comparison; byte_exact remains unknown. Original demo/SID/images are committed, with no license found. Disassembler opcode definitions acknowledge cc65 derivation.

decisions.title: LADS — reconstructed book-source assembler
decisions.reason: Reconstructs Richard Mansfield’s printed LADS assembler listings with OCR corrections, modern ca65 translation, machine/config overlays and object-code oracles. C64 generated source explicitly sets 6502 ISA and machine I/O equates; materialization scripts produce per-machine assembly/binary/disk artifacts. Root is substantive source reconstruction plus verification tooling; not simply a scanned-book archive. C64 VERIFY.txt reports 5,032 assembled bytes compared against a 4,986-byte oracle prefix, all matching. Do not call the entire binary byte-exact or independently verified. Disk images are documented as structurally validated but not emulator-boot-tested upstream. Apple from-source variant remains a study, with canonical decompiled variant retained. MIT applies only to original tools; reconstructed source/object code remains under original copyright. Raw book pages must be separately fetched.

decisions.title: virtnet.device — native AmigaOS 4 virtio network driver
decisions.reason: Native PowerPC SANA-II virtio-net-pci driver implementing legacy PCI transport, virtqueues, packet paths and Roadshow integration for AmigaOS 4.1. Source virtio.c implements I/O register access and device/queue setup; Makefile builds device.c plus virtio.c with ppc-amigaos-gcc. Upstream reports end-to-end TCP on QEMU sam460ex, approximately 24–25 Mbit/s with zero retransmissions in measured runs. Legacy/transitional virtio device supported; modern-only 0x1041 is not yet supported. Introductory multi-gigabit claims are generic aspirations; actual documented measurements are much lower and slower than the e1000 comparison. License says same as sibling virte1000 without a license file in this repository; licensing remains unresolved. Only QEMU testing is established upstream.

decisions.title: NetBSD rump — incomplete AmigaOS 4 network-stack port
decisions.reason: Substantive work-in-progress port provides PowerPC/AmigaOS adaptation for NetBSD rump kernel threads, memory, locks, timers and IPC, plus a socket-library shim architecture. Inspected osal_thread.c implements native Exec task creation/join and rump hypercall wrappers; fdtable.c deliberately provides an in-memory socket scaffold. Latest NEXT_STEPS.md supersedes stale README status: rump_init has been run, reaches about 15 adaptation-layer calls, then reproducibly faults in an OS4 library. Not a functioning TCP/IP stack. Real network dispatch, full BSD API and driver bridge are incomplete; documented deterministic DSI crash blocks initialization. Makefile/build reports prove only upstream partial compilation/symbol closure, not working networking. No local compilation or execution. CD32 is a conditional source option and is not claimed as a verified output here.

decisions.title: Ambermoon — original Amiga development-source snapshot
decisions.reason: Developer J. Horneman preserves a snapshot of Ambermoon 68000 assembly and contemporary data-format, design and localized-text documents. Selected MAIN.S and COMBAT.S contain real initialization, party-data handling, combat checks and combat-screen logic. README explicitly says the source is probably incomplete, probably not final, and cannot be transformed into a full game. Do not present it as a buildable release. README grants no license and says ownership of Thalion rights is unknown.

decisions.title: Habitat — original C64 client and Stratus server-source archive
decisions.reason: Museum restoration of the original Lucasfilm/QuantumLink Habitat archive contains the C64 macross client/art, Stratus VOS PL/I backend and historical tools/documents. Client Makefile invokes macross and slinky; comm_control.m implements actual host messages, region transitions and client response handling. Case-sensitive filesystem is required because some C64 source filenames differ only by case. README documents multiple source/binary vintages and missing tools including filldisk, loadrom and mtobin. Bundled binaries need not match nearby sources. C64 client depends on a compatible network/server environment; no modern server deployment or end-to-end playable setup was verified. Stratus VOS is archival backend context, not a newly claimed C64 runtime profile.

decisions.title: C64 SID players — recovered and disassembled music-driver sources
decisions.reason: Root collection of original and reverse-engineered C64 music players, including Rob Hubbard, Martin Galway and other named musicians. Selected Commando and Arkanoid assembly players contain driver implementation and music data; README aims to make each file produce a .sid using ACME. README warns some source may not assemble until cleaned up. No player was built or listened to. Repository MIT license is present, but ownership and permission for every historical player/tune were not independently established. A .sid output is consumed by a SID player; do not confuse host playback with a native full-game reconstruction.

decisions.title: CommLib2 — reconstructed C64 RS-232 communications library
decisions.reason: Reverse-engineered version of İlker Fıçıcılar’s CommLib2 RS-232 library with actual receive/transmit and setup assembly. Makefile uses KickAssembler through Docker and has c1541 disk-image packaging; README places code at $CA00 and receive buffer at $9000. BASIC users must reserve the receive buffer by reducing top-of-BASIC memory as documented; relocation is an upstream expectation, not verified. No license file was found in the inspected tree; original-library and reconstruction rights remain unclear.

decisions.title: skit — C64 emulator and reverse-engineering tool prototype
decisions.reason: C++ general C64 emulator/analysis project, rather than a wrapper dedicated to one game. Selected source constructs a 6510 CPU, 64 KiB RAM, BASIC/KERNAL/character ROMs, CIA and video devices; CPU source implements fetch, opcode execution, interrupt and debugging paths. Visual Studio 2010 project supplies Win32 configurations and SDL-related desktop build context. Upstream description calls it a slow C64 emulator intended to become a reverse-engineering tool. Completeness and timing accuracy were not independently tested. No root README or license was found. Bundled Commodore ROM images and third-party DLLs have separate unresolved redistribution rights.

decisions.title: mlxifier — C64 MLX II checksum-listing generator
decisions.reason: Small complete Rust command-line tool reimplementing Compute! MLX II checksums for C64 type-in listings. Source skips the two-byte PRG header, groups data into eight-byte blocks, zero-pads the final block and computes/emits address/data/checksum lines. No README or license file is present; arguments and usage were inferred from the inspected main function. Host Rust/Cargo utility, not native C64 code. No particular host OS support or checksum parity was tested.

decisions.title: Galactic Empire — native C64 game reconstruction in C
decisions.reason: C reconstruction of the original C64 Galactic Empire with actual galaxy generation, player/world/mission logic and graphics modules. Despite the Raspberry Pi name and metadata wording, the Makefile defaults to cc65 target c64 and builds a C64 executable; README describes running it in VICE on a Pi. Raspberry Pi is the emulator host, not the output ISA or a native ARM port. README names cc65 2.19 and VICE 3.5-era tooling. No license file was found and gameplay equivalence was not checked.

decisions.title: Blagger JS — C64 gameplay reconstruction for the browser
decisions.reason: Substantive JavaScript gameplay with player movement, collision, jump arcs, platforms, enemies, audio and canvas rendering; this is not a game-specific CPU emulator. Code labels movement rules with original 6502 addresses and distinguishes verified disassembly-derived behavior from tunable approximations; embedded assets identify a VICE snapshot as their source. The cited js/movement.md derivation file is not in the inspected two-file tree. Original data/assets are embedded and no license is present. Timing is explicitly described as not fully measured; source uses approximation/tuning notes. No runtime or fidelity test was performed.

decisions.title: AmigaED — Qt cross-development editor for Amiga software
decisions.reason: C++ Qt5/QScintilla cross-development editor with Amiga templates, vbcc/GCC selection and UAE startup integration. mainwindow.cpp implements compile/run and editor actions; qmake application.pro declares Qt widgets, print support and QScintilla dependencies. Experimental/example editor. README reports compiler failure for paths containing whitespace. BSD is only speculative upstream and is not included as supported. README uses a custom restricted public-domain-style statement with ideological use restrictions; Qt/QScintilla licenses apply separately. Do not summarize it as unrestricted public domain. This runs on modern host systems to create Amiga software; proposed AmigaOS4/AROS targets are roadmap items.

README claims an identical original binary; this is an upstream claim only and byte_exact stays unknown. Maintainer explicitly dedicates their comments/relocator work/builder to public domain, but describes original software’s public-domain status as best knowledge rather than a independently verified grant.

Training images are not included; Python preprocessing uses author-local absolute dataset paths. No license was found. The workload uses PCA; that alone is not evidence of AI-assisted development. Windows batch file points at a local cc65 installation; native runtime and any paddle/input requirements were not independently exercised.

decisions.title: ACEBasicJS — browser compiler and Amiga-inspired runtime

Compatibility is incremental and tied to documented seed programs, not full ACE/AmigaOS equivalence. No standalone license file was found in this repository; original ACE licensing should not automatically be copied to the new implementation.

README calls its Invaders demonstration complete, but inspected play-state code awards points on firing and simulates game over instead of full invader gameplay. Catalogue this as a development framework/prototype, not a verified complete game. No top-level license file was found. Build, tests and package outputs were not run. PET provenance does not establish a current PET target; current source explicitly says C64-only assembly.

decisions.title: Arlasoft C64 source collection — scope hold
decisions.reason: Overlapping collection retained as provenance, not independently counted. Uninspected unique unfinished/graphics-only portions remain potential future research, so this is not an exclusion of the entire corpus. README categorizes Complete, Partially Complete and Graphics Only folders; the complete recursive tree contains 6,048 entries. All ten standalone Arlasoft games reviewed in this pass have corresponding Complete folders. Nine have identical main-source blob SHAs; Merge64 has a differing main file but 56 identical blobs. This supports lineage collapse rather than separate collection/game counts. The collection also overlaps existing Caveman and Donkey Kong Junior entries and contains substantial unreviewed work-in-progress and graphics-only material. Hold as provenance/corpus inventory rather than a new umbrella project duplicating those games. Distinct unreviewed games may be investigated in a later focused pass. README requests no as-is unfinished preview releases and permits completion with credit. This is not a blanket open-source license; the isolated Graphics Only/Kye COPYING file does not license the corpus. Only README, complete tree, bounded history and exact-blob overlap were reviewed; the entire source corpus was not inspected. License: Informal author permission for completing WIP projects with credit and explicit objection to preview releases; no general license grant established.

decisions.title: Erasoft / RQ progs preservation archive — scope hold
decisions.reason: Hold at the demonstrated incomplete/binary-provenance scope; no project promoted. README provides author provenance, addresses and runtime notes for several games and tools; tree contains D64/D71/ZIP images, scans and screenshots rather than textual implementations. LICENSE explicitly says there is no source code because the programs were entered in machine language via the C128 monitor. It licenses that code under Apache-2.0, other assets under CC-BY-4.0, and specifically forbids reuse of ripped TMRT music/clouds. CHANGELOG documents binary-era fixes including load addresses, C128 bank setup and modified intros. README specifies NTSC origins and a True Drive Emulation caveat for The Race. Hold for binary-preservation provenance; do not promote as a source reconstruction merely because code is licensed. Disk contents were not extracted and no substantive machine-code disassembly was independently reviewed. Original unmodified binaries and cleaned-up variants are not interchangeable; changelog lists changes. Ripped assets and third-party recracks require careful rights separation. License: Code Apache-2.0; most assets CC-BY-4.0; explicitly excludes ripped TMRT music and BC’s Quest for Tires clouds.

decisions.title: Droid64 — scope hold
decisions.reason: Generic emulator implementations are visible, but Frodo family lineage remains collapsed with deferred vita64 rather than promoting another uncertain lineage record. README explicitly attributes the emulator to Christian Bauer's Frodo and says it was used nearly unchanged, with integration work. Older rosc77/Droid64 links are repository-name history, not another project. C64.cpp allocates a complete MOS6510/MOS6502-1541/VIC-II/SID/CIA/IEC/REU machine and copies embedded BASIC/Kernal/character/drive ROM arrays. CPUC64.cpp implements line-based CPU memory decoding and dispatches opcodes through CPU_emulline.h. Android build uses Gradle, Android SDK 23/build-tools 24.0.1, minSdk 15 and targetSdk 16. CMake 3.4.1 builds a shared Droid64 library from main, emu, pc and rom C++ directories. AudioControl.java uses Android AudioTrack; README describes OpenGL rendering, D64/T64 and zipped game archives. This is a generic emulator, not a game-specific emulation wrapper. The root Apache-2.0 notice does not resolve the licensing of the inherited Frodo core. The sister webOS port explicitly calls Frodo GPL; retain the mismatch rather than label all contents uniformly Apache-2.0. Embedded Commodore ROM arrays have separate redistribution rights; the app license does not establish those rights or game-archive rights. Build configuration contains a developer-specific signing path and obsolete Android toolchain versions; reproducibility on current tools is untested. Credential-like signing values were redacted from the evidence cache. Current-source files and 12 recent commit records inspected; last default-branch commit is in 2017 even though repository pushed_at is 2018. License: Root LICENSE and README state Apache-2.0; inherited Frodo and ROM rights unresolved. GitHub labels license NOASSERTION.

decisions.title: Frodo for webOS — scope hold
decisions.reason: Generic emulator implementations are visible, but Frodo family lineage remains collapsed with deferred vita64 rather than promoting another uncertain lineage record. README identifies Roland Schabenberger as porter and Christian Bauer as original Frodo author; generic C64 hardware emulation is confirmed by C64.cpp's chip/drive construction and CPUC64.cpp. src/Makefile defaults to LINEBASED/FRODO_PC and exposes a SINGLECYCLE/FRODO_SC alternative. generic.mak defaults PLATFORM=PALM and WEBOS=1, uses Palm PDK ARM GNU toolchains, SDL/SDL_ttf/SDL_image, GLES_CM and pdl; it also contains g++ Windows/Linux alternatives. manual.txt specifically describes HP TouchPad corners/touch areas, disk/tape browsing, joystick-port switching and optional true 1541 emulation. No standalone license file appears in the complete tree. README asserts GPL without an exact version; source headers attribute Christian Bauer. Bundled resources contain 1541.ROM, Basic.ROM, Char.ROM and Kernal.ROM; their rights remain separate. Palm PDK, dated compiler/deployment assumptions, and mixed host-specific commands mean current reproducibility is not established. webOS is absent from the baseline platform-label set. Preserve webOS in runtime notes rather than introduce a new platform label or relabel it Android/Amiga. License: README says GPL (version unspecified); no complete license text found in tree. ROM rights unresolved.

decisions.title: SID FX Editor/Player prototype — scope hold
decisions.reason: Hold at the demonstrated incomplete/binary-provenance scope; no project promoted. README's detailed status limits completion to phases 1-2; phases 3-6 (editor UI, input, live editing, multi-slot management/file I/O) remain planned despite the opening 'complete' description. sid-player.kc contains three-voice SID register writes, frequency interpolation, filter settings, raster-IRQ setup, FX bank and start/stop API; main.kc implements only keyboard-driven explosion/laser/coin demonstrations. Makefile compiles only src/main.kc with KickC -t c64basic -O2. test-effects.kc is a prerequisite, but main.kc does not include it or call its five extra effect initializers, so 'eight effects' is not the actual wired demo scope. The IRQ handler's acknowledgement block writes VIC_RASTER, defined as $D012; IRQ installation uses a raw $FFFE vector. These are concrete source locations requiring hardware/banking validation, not independently reproduced failures. Comments claim 14 bytes per voice and 48 bytes per FX slot, while the listed primitive byte/word fields and padding do not substantiate that layout. No sizeof/assertion or generated-map evidence was found to reconcile it. The single returned commit explicitly names Claude as both author and committer, and the default branch also begins claude/. This supports Claude attribution only, not a further Claude Code/model claim. No build, emulator run, SID listening test, cycle measurement, PAL/NTSC timing validation, or memory-layout validation was performed. make test prints that manual testing is required; it is not an automated correctness suite. Frequency sweeps use frame counts; advertised PAL/NTSC and <500-cycle performance remain upstream claims. README license section is a placeholder asking the author to choose a license, not a grant. No license file exists in the complete tree. License: Unlicensed/undetermined: README contains '[Choose your license: MIT, GPL, Public Domain, etc.]'; no actual license grant identified. Explicit AI attribution: Claude. Explicit Claude name is the attribution basis. Branch name corroborates but does not independently establish product/model. Do not infer Claude Code from provider address.

FormatIFF.cpp implements IFF ILBM header/palette/bitplane loading plus saving; FormatIFF.h declares FORM/ILBM/BMHD/CMAP/BODY and auxiliary chunk identifiers. Painter's project file directly references this repository-shaped P:\Common hierarchy, including Grafik\ImageFormate\FormatIFF.cpp. No root README, root license text or independent build project was found in the complete tree; the verified consumer is Painter. No repository-wide license grant was established. Third-party libraries and source notices must remain separately attributed. CAMG handling is skipped, so special Amiga display-mode support cannot be inferred from generic IFF handling. Broad host portability and build completeness were not validated; no direct C64-specific format implementation was established. License: No root LICENSE/README grant found; no license assigned to repository as a whole.

decisions.title: AmiFTP 2 — restored native Amiga FTP client
decisions.reason: README documents GUI transfers, Aminet mode, ARexx scripting, transfer resume and PASV/PORT support; ftp.c implements socket connection, command/reply, send/receive and passive fallback paths. The SAS/C smakefile links ReAction, rtasl.lib and tcp.lib with the UI/FTP implementation; AS225 support is disabled in the current documented version. README requires AmigaOS 3.2 with ReAction; older ClassAct systems are only described as possible. External SDK/toolchain assignments and link libraries must be supplied. No secure-FTP/TLS functionality or security audit is established by this review. Top-level MIT terms do not erase the legacy four-clause Berkeley notice retained in ftp.c.

decisions.title: IFFTools — native Amiga image and audio converters
decisions.reason: image_decoder.c contains concrete bitplane extraction and IFF bitmap decoding; sound_decoder.c implements sound decompression/conversion paths. SMakefile builds iffpicture.lib, iffsound.lib and two conversion commands; bundled libpng/zlib are dependencies rather than extra projects. README lists a broad format matrix, but not every advertised variant was independently audited or exercised. Requires Amiga SDK/SAS/C setup, libpng/zlib dependencies and Amiga library interfaces. No independent corpus-conformance tests; bundled data and third-party dependency notices need their own rights checks.

decisions.title: BGUI — preserved Amiga BOOPSI GUI framework
decisions.reason: baseclass.c implements BOOPSI object creation/render/layout/interaction and retains long historical RCS change notes; bgui_init.c opens native Amiga library dependencies. SAS/C build has standard/debug/enhanced variants; enhanced explicitly selects CPU=68020, while historical build notes say the standard build supports OS 2/68000. Historical standard-build compatibility is a documented claim, not a tested current deployment profile. AROS support is visible in conditional source/build layout, but no new AROS platform label or tested AROS runtime is claimed. LICENSE.md is BSD-3-Clause, while LICENSE has an older use/copy permission notice; retain both and per-file copyrights rather than asserting uniform relicensing.

decisions.title: ClassAction — restored Amiga file manager
decisions.reason: Main C++ source implements ReAction file-manager setup, actions and library initialization. smakefile states missing Global/ IniFile and StringList sources were reconstructed from the 4.6 object API; concrete replacements are present. Current build embeds relocated resource objects through generated ClassAction_res_embed.c because original StormC resource objects have relocations rejected by SAS/C. This is partial source restoration, not a clean all-source rebuild: object inputs remain required for resource regeneration. Documented AmigaOS 3.5/3.9 and resource.library/popupmenu/xadmaster/xfdmaster dependencies must be supplied. Historical binary distribution was mailware with noncommercial/no-alteration restrictions; source publication and preservation do not establish a standard open-source license.

decisions.title: gtlayout.library — preserved Amiga GadTools layout toolkit
decisions.reason: LTP_LayoutGadgets.c contains the substantial native gadget layout implementation and optional BOOPSI class loading. SAS/C smakefile compiles the source suite and generates documentation/header material; current CPU setting is ANY, with old 68020 option commented out. README’s future AROS/MorphOS porting intent is not an implemented runtime claim. SAS/C 6.58, NDK 3.2R4, ctags, LibDescConverter and Autodoc are documented dependencies. The source is marked freely distributable; that is not automatically equivalent to a modern permissive license.

decisions.title: iffparse and iffar — Amiga IFF inspection and archive tools
decisions.reason: main.c parses/displays IFF chunk metadata through Amiga iffparse.library and supports file/clipboard modes. iff.c and companion archive sources preserve an iffar lineage based on Karl Lehenbauer’s public-domain 1988 EA IFF code, ported to Amiga DOS I/O/C89. SMakefile builds iffparse and iffar as one related command suite. The repository name must not be mistaken for a recreation of Commodore’s iffparse.library. BUILD.md calls the default CPU 68020, but inspected SCOPTIONS/SMakefile do not enforce an explicit CPU flag; retain this as documented intent. SAS/C 6.58 and NDK 3.2R4 are required; no independent parsing/round-trip corpus validation.

decisions.title: LZXa — Amiga LZX-compatible archive reimplementation
decisions.reason: README describes an independent reimplementation of LZX 1.21; inspected code contains hash-chain LZ77 encoding, bitstream decompression and real command parsing. vbcc +aos68k_posix build emits lzx and libalzx.a; HOST=1 switches to a C89 host build for smoke testing. The decoder header explicitly says it is ported from unlzx.c logic, and README credits UnLZX2/amiga-lzx cross-checks; preserve that lineage rather than certifying clean-room independence. README’s clean-room and tested-on-Amiga assertions are upstream claims, not independently certified facts. It decodes merged groups but writes separate streams; no LHA/LZH, multivolume or recursive directory walking. Several compatibility switches are parsed as no-ops. No archive interchange, byte equivalence, compression quality or damaged-file behavior was independently tested.

decisions.title: SDL — native PowerPC AmigaOS4 multimedia port
decisions.reason: SDL_os4video.c creates the native AmigaOS4 SDL video device and connects display/window/event/OpenGL backend functions. Makefile.amigaos4 uses ppc-amigaos GCC and produces SDL3 static/shared libraries and preferences tooling; current docs require AmigaOS 4.1 Final Edition. The older SDL2-AmigaOS4 repository explicitly redirects here and remains lineage-only rather than a second candidate. Current AmigaOS4 docs state configure/CMake are unsupported; use the dedicated makefile, not generic SDL build assumptions. Altivec disabled; Camera/GPU/Haptic/Pen/Power/Sensor and Vulkan backends unsupported per current docs. Compositing geometry has limitations. No generic SDL host platforms are added merely because upstream SDL supports them; this candidate is the Amiga port.

decisions.title: ILBMToIcon — Amiga icon-format converter
decisions.reason: ilbmtoicon.c contains concrete IFF ILBM/ByteRun1/chunk and icon serialization logic with libpng/zlib dependencies. README distinguishes old-style/pre3.5 image data, appended IFF ICON data and PNG icon output. Makefile uses HOST_CC; CMake also advertises m68k-amigaos packaging and builds infoinfo as companion utility. Output icon format and development target are Amiga; portable host build is not a claim of execution on every OS. No independent format compatibility or icon rendering test; input artwork rights remain the user’s responsibility.

decisions.title: CAMD I2C — native Amiga MIDI transmit driver
decisions.reason: camd-i2c.c implements CAMD callback handling and SendI2C at default address 0x42; main.c defines the resident driver entry points. CMake builds a freestanding driver with -m68040 and fetches i2c.library through CPM. Hardware and i2c.library are required; no particular attached MIDI device or working hardware configuration was independently verified. The inspected implementation establishes transmit functionality, not a complete bidirectional MIDI hardware stack. Bundled source is small but concrete; it is not a generic Amiga keyword-only hit.

decisions.title: Poseidon USB — standalone AmigaOS3 source restoration
decisions.reason: Main library source contains the full USB stack implementation; OS3 class_startup.c provides resident startup/open/close/expunge glue. upstream/aros.json pins the imported AROS commit and relocation map; src/LEGAL records Hodges’s 2009 AROS Public License release. Makefile builds OS3 library, class modules, GUI/tools and release packaging from source; components stay one stack candidate. Upstream explicitly says linked OS3 binaries still need real runtime validation, despite build checks. AROS hardware-controller code is retained but not staged for OS3; old closed E3B drivers, PsdLoadModule/PsdRestart and other unreleased pieces are absent. A complete compatible USB setup remains required; this is not a tested drop-in complete historical release.

decisions.title: ZZ9000 — native AmigaOS driver suite
decisions.reason: Network device.c implements native SANA-II Amiga driver dispatch and hardware access; rtg/mntgfx-gcc.c implements graphics-card integration. README identifies the original MNT source and independent fork status, with firmware and ARM-side logic in separate repositories. Top-level build invokes pinned Amiga toolchain workflows; net/Makefile sets68020 and includes host-side test targets elsewhere in the suite. A reviewed code-fix commit explicitly credits Codex review; attribution is limited to review assistance. Requires ZZ9000 ZorroII/III hardware; ZZ9000AX audio and Picasso96/USB/network dependencies vary by component. Matched firmware/bitstream/SDK versions matter, especially ZorroII memory-layout negotiation; driver source alone does not provide a complete setup. The board’s ARM coprocessors are not the CPU executing the Amiga-side network driver; retain separate roles. No independent hardware/runtime/test execution; original MNT lineage is one family, not an extra project count.

decisions.title: ProTrackerTools — Amiga MOD optimization and conversion
decisions.reason: Serializer.cs parses sample headers, song order, four-channel pattern data and M.K./M!K! signatures, and serializes modules back. P61Convert.cs contains actual sample/pattern cleanup and P61 packing; OptiMod is the same toolkit’s frontend, not a separate entry. Projects target .NET Framework 4.8, with Windows Forms frontend and AnyCPU managed build. Amiga is the module-format/development relationship; Windows is the inspected executable host. No standalone license in the complete tree or explicit license grant in inspected source/README; source visibility is not an open-source permission. No byte-exact round-trip, playback or P61 runtime compatibility was tested; input music/sample rights separate.

decisions.title: wav2amiga — ProTracker sample preparation
decisions.reason: MainForm.cs resamples via NAudio MediaFoundation, extracts the high byte of 16-bit PCM and writes raw sample files. Stacked modes align samples to 256-byte ProTracker offset boundaries; csproj targets .NET Framework 4.8/Windows Forms. This prepares Amiga tracker assets on Windows; it is not an Amiga-native executable. The resampling code retains the source channel count despite a monoSource variable name; do not promise automatic stereo-to-mono conversion. No license file in the tree; NAudio/Newtonsoft are external dependencies with separate terms. No output playback or sample fidelity testing.

decisions.title: TTE Track Loaders — native Amiga floppy loading
decisions.reason: ttetrack.asm and tteturbo.asm implement CIA/custom-chip floppy DMA, MFM decoding, sector checks and retries. Turbo uses two MFM buffers so decompression can overlap disk DMA; both contain a 68000 ZX0 decompressor and credit Frank Wille loader lineage. Headers document drive-number selection as not implemented. External hardware include files such as hw.i/intbits.i/cia.i and a suitable assembler/integration harness are required; no standalone makefile is present. Embedded ZX0 code has a zlib-style grant, but no clear top-level license covering the entire loader suite was found. No PAL/NTSC, accelerator/cache or physical floppy behavior was independently verified.

decisions.title: TTE Disk Builder — Amiga bootable ADF authoring
decisions.reason: Program.cs writes a 1024-byte bootblock, 16-byte file-table entries at 0x400, packed payloads and pads to 0xDC000 bytes; it calculates the boot checksum. It invokes external Windows packers and targets .NET Framework 4.7.2; input bootblock and selected compressor executables are separate prerequisites. Existing decision markyturtle-ttedisbuilder-netcore-port excludes a .NET Core port as separate lineage. This original upstream utility is not currently a project and does not reverse that fork exclusion. No original bootblock is supplied; a compatible 1024-byte bootblock and disk manifest are required. Source invokes shrinkler.exe, salvador.exe, zopfli.exe and optional other packers; tool availability is not verified. No explicit project-wide license in tree; bootblock/data and compressor rights are separate. No image boot, loader interoperability or output checksum test performed.

decisions.title: amigazen/toolkit
decisions.reason: SDK distribution/collection with many shipped binaries, headers and existing component copies. No distinct source implementation selected for a new project; keep as collection discovery source. Its Codex name refers to an Amiga C lint tool, not evidence of OpenAI Codex use.

decisions.title: djh0ffman/xmtools
decisions.reason: Substantive Windows/.NET XM serialization and injector source, but README ties it to an XMPlay tracker-music demonstration; inspected source does not establish actual Amiga or C64 implementation/development relevance. Shared author alone is insufficient.

decisions.title: amigaports/sdl2-amigaos4
decisions.reason: Older SDL2 AmigaOS4 repository directs users to AmigaPorts/SDL. Preserve lineage; do not count a second multimedia-library port family.

decisions.title: Return of Medusa / Rings of Medusa II
decisions.reason: Approved repository-level discovery with substantive source. Original 1991 Atari ST/Amiga C and assembly published by the original author, with a later author-maintained C/SDL3 modernization. Neither preservation nor the source port establishes independent reverse engineering. Original-language fields retain C and m68k assembly; modern gameplay is C, while historical assembly remains preserved. Original tag resolves to commit 036364ccebfcb5724f8581260db683d289336dc1; retain one repository-level record for original and SDL3 lineage. All four build flags remain null; source and overall audit remain partial. Root-normalized screening passed the supplied 1665-project baseline and 1951-prior-root union.

decisions.title: MemSnap — restored Amiga memory-use monitor
decisions.reason: Approved substantive repository-level tooling discovery. MemSnap is the maintained restoration of Martin W. Scott’s 1992/1993 memory-use utility. README identifies the original Aminet memsnap2 package, while source/memsnap.c implements the native window/menu interface and chip/fast/total-memory snapshots. The restoration adds peak-memory reporting; original package and restoration are one counted lineage. Canonical root https://github.com/amigaports/memsnap was absent from the fresh 1665-project baseline at 2d051f4d3b5bbc17a19b6537aef9a8671411901d; prior review also screened the 1951-root union. Inspected snapshot: cd44277a51a1129b4b29ce12d38f602ab6b467cc. A source-restoration tooling record with a memory-profiling capability, rather than a recovered game or a new binary decompilation. The C implementation measures free memory before and after a snapshot to help observe program allocations and leaks; the current README explicitly records the restored release’s peak column and CMake build system. CMakeLists.txt declares CMake 2.8.5 and C11, rejects non-Amiga builds and configures the native utility with small-code/base-relative options. It also calls target_link_options, added in CMake 3.13, so the advertised 2.8.5 minimum is internally inconsistent. This is a source-reviewed recipe defect, not a failed compilation result; no compiler/toolchain invocation was attempted. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, execution, gameplay or byte-comparison was performed. License/asset caveat: README reproduces original author’s public-domain statement; bundled tracers fonts require separate provenance review. UUID standards compatibility is an upstream claim that was not tested. The library recipe requires CMake 3.14.0, uses -m68020 and freestanding/no-standard-library/no-startfiles linking, supplies the native entry point and installs uuid.library plus developer material. The source list includes time/random generation and name-based SHA-1 support. The get_verstring helper and Amiga development setup must be available; no complete build, utility execution or standards-conformance test was attempted. The i2clib40 compatibility comment and I2C naming comment are copied-text caveats, not established dependencies or compatibility results. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, execution, gameplay or byte-comparison was performed. The default TARGETS value enables libdebug.a while commenting out libddebug.a; the parallel-output path is incomplete and its input function returns -1. No archive was independently compiled or linked, and the disabled/incomplete parallel path is not treated as equivalent to the serial implementation. README explicitly lists unsupported nested functions and not-really-functional stacktracing, so those capabilities are not promoted. The make recipe uses ppc-amigaos GCC or native AmigaOS compilation, STABS debug information and -lauto. It links setbreak.o from a rule requiring setbreak.s, but the complete non-truncated snapshot tree contains setbreak.h and no setbreak.s. This leaves the documented make route incomplete. No build was attempted, and the missing input is not converted into a measured compilable=false result. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, execution, gameplay or byte-comparison was performed. A reimplemented compiler/library-interface tool, generating FD files, C prototypes, inlines/pragmas, proto headers, LVO files, C stubs and gateway glue. The supported classic AmigaOS, OS4, MorphOS, AROS and Amithlon backends are development targets of one Perl generator, not independent runnable ports of a legacy application. The configure/make setup assembles and installs a Perl-based generator, and sfdc.readme explicitly lists Perl as required. Reviewed main.pl and generator modules implement the input processing and emitted interfaces. No installation, execution, generated-header comparison or emitted-ABI validation was performed. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, execution, gameplay or byte-comparison was performed. License/asset caveat: main.pl declares GPL-2.0-or-later; COPYING includes GPL-2.0.

decisions.title: SDI headers — Amiga compiler and ABI compatibility macros
decisions.reason: Approved substantive repository-level tooling discovery. SDI is a maintained set of C headers for compiler differences, hooks, interrupts, shared libraries, varargs and related compatibility helpers. SDI_lib.h and SDI_compiler.h implement platform/compiler-specific ABI macros, and the repository includes source examples. README version 1.7 (2015) predates version strings within current headers; it is not a current all-files version declaration. Canonical root https://github.com/adtools/sdi was absent from the fresh 1665-project baseline at 2d051f4d3b5bbc17a19b6537aef9a8671411901d; prior review also screened the 1951-root union. Inspected snapshot: 423bdb30121988e17cfdc831d93b9d844470d748. Cross-platform compiler/ABI development support, not a complete compiler or SDK and not a standalone runnable application. Implemented headers plus library examples justify a tooling record. Canonical Amiga/MorphOS filters preserve the native OS3, OS4 and MorphOS consumer variants in notes rather than implying all are classic-Amiga binaries. The package supplies headers and source examples with OS3/OS4/MorphOS make routes. Inspected OS3/OS4 examples pass -I../../includes, while the checked snapshot has headers at repository root, so include-layout/installation adjustments may be required. Target SDK headers and compilers are separate dependencies. No example was compiled, and portability across every documented compiler was not independently tested. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, execution, gameplay or byte-comparison was performed. License/asset caveat: README and header comments explicitly dedicate headers/examples to public domain.

decisions.title: agrigaatti/alien-breed-3d-i
decisions.reason: Substantial modernized AB3D I build, but README/main source expressly derive from original Team17 sources in videogamepreservation/alienbreed3dii and RTG work in mheyer32/ab3d-rtg. decisions.title: dirkwhoffmann/vamiga
decisions.reason: Fresh root and substantive canonical native macOS emulator, but tracked vAmigaNet/vAmigaNet and vAmigaDOS/vAmigaDOS already share its core. Conservatively hold pending catalogue family/independent-product decision rather than double-count code lineage. Reviewed Blitter.cpp implementation, C++20 Core/CMakeLists, About, GettingStarted and LICENSE. It is the native canonical Amiga500/1000/2000 emulator, not a binary-only wrapper or unchanged mirror. Native macOS app documentation specifies macOS12+. Portable C++20 core/headless target has CMake3.16+, optional zlib and host dependencies. Nothing built. Current LICENSE distinguishes GPL-3.0-or-later application, MPL-2.0 Core, MIT Moira CPU. Older manual discussion is less specific. Needs a licensed Kickstart or bundled AROS alternative; application/game disks separate.

decisions.title: bisc67/monster
decisions.reason: Substantive historical monitor source and explicit Amiga branches exist, but README only says Atari/Amiga debugger; default MONITOR.S selects AtariST=1/Amiga=0, DEBUG.S warns about Devpac3 assembly problems and attributes most code only to 'author of lemmings'.
