decisions.title: Amiga DirectMedia Layer
decisions.reason: Substantive native video/control/timer abstraction is present, including m68k chunky-to-planar assembly and AGA/CyberGraphX code, but the intended standalone interface/runtime scope is underdocumented and the WarpOS branch adds only src/ppc/ with an empty .gitkeep. Retain as a lead; do not imply a verified PowerPC port. AGA and RTG/CyberGraphX are alternative code paths, not universal hardware minima. The 040 converter filename is not proof of a universal 68040 requirement.

decisions.title: RDBParser
decisions.reason: MIT-licensed C++20 Rigid Disk Block/partition reader is real source, but upstream explicitly calls it a debugger-driven code example. Keep as a focused format-analysis lead rather than inflate this substantive-tools batch. Source only opens the supplied file/device for reading; it is not a disk repair utility. CMake downloads an unpinned AROS hardblocks.h at configure time. Windows/Mac examples are suggested uses; Linux-oriented netinet/in.h code is present and no Windows build was verified. The Amiga RDB data format does not establish a m68k CPU for this host tool.

decisions.title: ptplayer convenience mirror
decisions.reason: README explicitly identifies this as a third-party convenience mirror of Frank Wille’s canonical Aminet ptplayer. Keep provenance; do not count the mirror as a newly independent project. Native replay source is substantial and version 6.3 is present; source-reviewed only. The same dependency is already referenced by tracked Amiga projects; separate canonical-project review can be considered later.

decisions.title: TOSEMU — Atari TOS original-binary userspace runner
decisions.reason: Approved original-binary runner discovery. TOSEMU is Johan Toverland Thelin’s hosted environment for original Atari TOS executables, not a decompilation of one guest application. The current PRG loader opens and maps the supplied file, checks magic 0x601A, constructs the guest environment and applies relocation entries. The tosemu executable runs a program directly; the separate tosaesd daemon supports shared GEM accessory sessions and is not a prerequisite for a single CLI invocation. README explicitly targets integration into Linux and excludes general games/demos. This repository is counted once; its hosted EmuTOS and Musashi components are dependencies, not additional runner discoveries. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot 443340b2dfcf9e691a080bc4e3722102bc9c2839, non-truncated tree with 274 entries. README requires recursive Musashi and EmuTOS submodules and make; Makefile uses GCC, generates Musashi opcode tables and links hosted EmuTOS AES/VDI. NO_WAYLAND=1 removes the Wayland/xkbcommon headers, libraries and protocol-generation route; the Ubuntu workflow explicitly uses it for check and emuvdi-check. The GUI route needs Wayland tooling; optional detected integrations include D-Bus, libpng, FreeType/fontconfig and ALSA. The hosted EmuTOS build uses -fno-strict-aliasing and non-PIE flags because guest APIs contain 32-bit pointer fields. Devpac/Lattice tests are separate from building the host runner and require the original installations. Upstream describes excluding SoftFloat and dead-stripping unused later-CPU FPU/MMU code; this review did not inspect a resulting binary or certify link-time license composition. All four build flags remain null; inspected recipes and upstream reports are not local test results.

decisions.title: ParaTos — Atari TOS and MiNT userspace runner
decisions.reason: Approved original-binary runner discovery. ParaTos is an experimental direct runner for original Atari TOS/MiNT command-line applications. README identifies Linux and explains the system-call translation approach. gemdos/loader.c reads and endian-converts the PRG header, builds the basepage/environment, copies text/data, applies relocation fixups and appends ARGV data. paratos.c loads the named executable and enters the CPU engine directly, without an ST machine boot. A 2023 upstream commit explicitly added OSX support, and current Apple-specific executable-path and byte-order code remains present; this refines the earlier discovery’s Linux-only evidence without asserting that a modern macOS build was tested. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot 9d43e70bce3ed4f82ee43e35375994332fc2ac4b, non-truncated tree with 106 entries. CMakeLists.txt declares CMake 3.10, C11, bundled mushashi and gemdos subdirectories and a paratos executable. Clang warning adjustments and the later explicit opcode-table definitions document maintenance of that route; they do not prove current build success. The original OSX-support commit adds Apple byte order and executable-path logic, with guarded host API differences, retained at the inspected tip. The guest test directory requires make plus a m68k-atari-mintelf- cross-toolchain and produces hello.tos, echo_args.tos, exit_code.tos and syscall proxies. Those generated guest outputs are ignored build artifacts, not prebuilt executables present in the tree. No boot-ROM dependency appears in the direct loader/build recipe. The host virtual-memory and unaligned-access assumptions require validation on any selected platform. All four build flags remain null; inspected recipes and upstream reports are not local test results.

decisions.title: riscose — RISC OS ARM userspace binary runner
decisions.reason: Approved original-binary runner discovery. One riscose project family is tracked across its original SourceForge home, repo.or.cz lineage and the inspected hamishcoleman/riscose GitHub tree. The original site describes SWI-level execution of unmodified RISC OS applications without a RISC OS ROM. README demonstrates direct GNU grep invocation with host stdin and filenames. Current main.c and mem.c load an application image at guest address 0x8000 and execute it through arm_run_routine. Although README still says Absolute executables only, current code and man/riscose.1 also expose module and utility modes; this is evidence of implemented paths, not complete compatibility. The GitHub tip is 2023-10-25; a prior indexed repo.or.cz summary reported 2023-11-02, but its direct access was geographically blocked. That lineage is retained without pretending the GitHub tip is the newest commit anywhere in the family. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot ec85f120327ce37ecee8bbcb90f3111330bd5bae, non-truncated tree with 231 entries. The inspected route is Autotools plus C: a Git checkout needs maintainer tools, configure checks a C compiler, yacc, ranlib, awk and Perl, and src/Makefile.am links ncurses and readline. The checked-in Ubuntu workflow installs autoconf/libgdbm-dev, runs autoreconf -if, then configure and make; the workflow is a recipe, not a successful run verified here. ARMulator is the default backend, with sleeve/native selectable. The generated rom/romimage.o belongs to the compatibility runtime and is not evidence that an original RISC OS boot ROM is required. The original project explicitly says no RISC OS ROM is needed. Guest compiler tools are separate inputs, and the original test page explicitly withholds redistribution of Norcroft cc. No build, guest execution or binary-equivalence experiment was performed. All four build flags remain null; inspected recipes and upstream reports are not local test results.

decisions.title: riscose lineage alias: https://riscose.sourceforge.net/
decisions.reason: Original riscose site documents ROM-free SWI compatibility, historical Linux/ARM work, GPL distribution and the dated 2001 Norcroft cc/Acorn linker demonstration. It is provenance for the single riscose record, not a second runner. Historical pages do not establish present-day compatibility. Keep one counted family; do not promote this location separately.

decisions.title: riscose lineage alias: https://repo.or.cz/riscose.git
decisions.reason: Known alternate riscose repository lineage, retained under the same project identity as SourceForge and the inspected GitHub copy. The discovery pass observed an indexed 2023-11-02 summary but direct retrieval was geographically restricted; no bypass was attempted and the repository’s exact current head has not been verified. Keep one counted family; do not promote this location separately.

decisions.title: mpw — original 68K MPW tool runner for macOS
decisions.reason: Approved source-reviewed original-binary runner discovery. README identifies the mpw command, author, tool-search layout and native-shell invocation. toolbox/loader.cpp opens the original resource fork, loads CODE resource 0, constructs the A5/jump-table state and brings in additional CODE segments. This is a substantive original-tool runner, not a source-port compiler or a script around a fully booted Mac. Root and record ID are absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior dedup index. Inspected master tip: a6b58bf3828e78388ab70ce53bf7be7bbff19d18. Tooling with emulator and development-environment capabilities. The loader executes original guest instructions; toolbox/dispatch.cpp translates Classic Mac OS Open/Read/Write traps, and toolbox/os.cpp plus mpw/mpw_io.cpp route guest I/O into host-backed FDEntry operations. API reimplementation and embedded CPU emulation are distinct parts of the same runner. No full-Mac, arbitrary-tool or full-API compatibility is established. README credits the WinFellow 680x0 core under GPL-2.0-or-later and describes the combined executable as GPL v2. The public-domain mempoolite/SQLite-derived allocator and BSD-style notices in examined MPW I/O code retain their component distinctions; libsane is a separate submodule. Original MPW tools, interfaces, runtime libraries and other guest content are not licensed by the emulator grant. This 68K implementation is separate from Treeki’s Rust/PowerPC mpw-emu; similar names and purpose do not establish a code fork. Overall source/author/dependency graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: mpw-emu — experimental PowerPC MPW tool runner
decisions.reason: Approved source-reviewed original-binary runner discovery. src/main.rs reads the requested original tool through MacFile, parses its PEF data fork and resources, links it into emulated memory, forwards argv and returns the emulated exit status. README reports MWCPPC from CodeWarrior Pro 1 and DeRez results. These are upstream demonstrations, not independent compatibility tests; this record is the experimental runner rather than CodeWarrior/MPW itself. Root and record ID are absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior dedup index. Inspected main tip: a0d23d515987ae5b486da9430e0b78a02ac93b4f. Substantive emulator/development tooling: src/linker.rs builds transition-vector shims for imported symbols; src/emulator/mod.rs installs InterfaceLib/StdCLib and Toolbox/C-library callbacks and handles them through a PowerPC supervisor-call hook. Original PEF instructions run inside Unicorn without booting Classic Mac OS. Missing imports remain logged, the initialization vector is explicitly unimplemented, and the README lists missing PEF relocations and APIs. XCOFF support is not established. The complete 37-entry tree has no LICENSE/COPYING grant, Cargo.toml has no license field, and repository metadata reports license null. Do not describe it as permissively licensed or assume public source authorizes redistribution. Unicorn and Rust dependencies retain their separate terms, as do original CodeWarrior/MPW executables and libraries. README’s comparison with SheepShaver/QEMU describes the purpose; no fork relationship is established. Merged PR #1 concerns Retro68-produced MacBinary II input and is not evidence that Retro68 is this runner’s implementation or guest CPU. Overall source/author/dependency graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: MS-DOS Player — original DOS command runner for Windows
decisions.reason: Approved source-reviewed original-binary runner discovery. readme.txt explicitly targets 16-bit DOS command-line utilities and demonstrates msdos lcc sample.c followed by msdos sample.exe. msdos.cpp identifies Takeda as author, loads MZ/ZM EXEs with relocation and otherwise uses the COM entry at 0x100. The selected maintained source root is cracyc/msdos-player, default branch vt. Its README credits imported fixes from the cracyc fork; the official Takeda distribution is lineage/context, not a second project. Root and record ID are absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior dedup index. Inspected vt tip: b3ebaa8452be478afec604361db32e9451eb43e2. Emulator/development tooling with CPU execution plus DOS/BIOS service translation. The INT 21h dispatch sends 3Dh/3Fh/40h/4Bh to host-backed open/read/write/execute handling. The direct console workflow does not boot a DOS disk image, but this is not a CPU-only layer: text-mode hardware scaffolding, memory services and optional driver/VDD support exist. README excludes Win16, graphics/sound hardware and gaming as the project’s goal; protected-mode capabilities vary by CPU build. One family combines Takeda’s MS-DOS Player and the cracyc maintained fork; GitHub fork=false is hosting metadata and does not negate the documented lineage. README licenses source under GPL v2 and credits MAME CPU cores, Neko Project 21/W, DOSBox/DOSBox-X, DOSVAXJ3 and ReactOS-derived portions; component notices need preservation. Guest DOS compilers, commands, libraries and COMMAND.COM retain separate rights and must be supplied lawfully. This is neither Microsoft’s original NTVDM nor davidly/ntvdm. The official Takeda URL was retained from prior discovery, but this publication recheck received HTTP 403 and therefore does not newly verify its release/test claims. Overall source/author/dependency graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: Apout — original PDP-11 Unix a.out runner
decisions.reason: Approved source-reviewed original-binary runner discovery. The canonical DoctorWkt repository supplies the current Apout 2.4 source and identifies supported historical Unix binary families. main.c accepts an original pdp11_binary and arguments; aout.c identifies a.out magic/ABI, loads instructions and data and supports 2.11BSD overlays. Original commands and compiler binaries are guest inputs, not restored native-host sources. Root and record ID are absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior dedup index. Inspected master tip: bd9af21bd8bb2fa956dcda5db0b0aeec2cffc8f7. Emulator/development tooling: cpu.c fetches and dispatches original PDP-11 instructions, while v7trap.c directly implements guest read/write/open through native calls and bsdtrap.c provides a separate 2.11BSD ABI. APOUT_ROOT rewrites absolute guest paths; relative paths remain host-relative. This is not a full PDP-11 machine or guest OS boot. It provides host-file access, not containment; NATIVES is enabled by the Makefile and unrecognized binaries can be attempted with host execv. The current repository has a GPL-3.0 LICENSE and GitHub identifies GPL-3.0; COPYRIGHT also preserves permissive notices for Warren Toomey and Eric Edwards’ instruction-emulation ancestry. Keep this mixed file-level provenance explicit rather than copying an older mirror’s permissive-only summary or asserting that every inherited line was relicensed. Historical guest Unix executables/libraries and disk collections require their own rights review. Older Apout mirrors/ports are this lineage’s context and are not separately promoted; no macOS/Windows current-support guarantee is borrowed from them. Overall source/author/dependency graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: run68x — Human68k command-line executable runner
decisions.reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. run68x is the maintained Human68k CUI emulator derived from run68. The README names rururutan/run68 and several run68mac forks as origins. The current C implementation has its own executable loader, 68000 interpreter, debugger and Human68k-compatible services. One family is counted; original run68 and the linked macOS variants are lineage references, not additional discoveries. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: fc28826dd795b1f0a3241f0b03fe2353e12e7233. Modern tooling executes original Human68k .X and raw .R programs from argv, using host files and the existing terminal. load.c reads the HU header, performs relocation and initializes BSS; run68.c builds a PSP and enters the interpreter. DOS calls, IOCS and FE floating-point helpers are implemented in host C. The initialized HUMAN.SYS name represents a synthetic PSP, not a required OS image. The inspected direct-run path needs no original ROM or booted Human68k. README and source headers license run68x under GPL-2.0-or-later and explicitly trace run68/run68mac ancestry. The family is counted once under kg68k/run68x; alternate forks may differ in API and platform support. Original Human68k tools, XC-linked executables and their data remain separately licensed. The high-memory mode requires users to patch linked XC library code themselves; no automatic patcher or right to redistribute original tools is implied. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: m68 — CP/M-68K and 68000 executable runner
decisions.reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. m68 directly loads 68000 CP/M-68K .68K, Linux-style ELF and Motorola hex programs. The repository contains a substantial custom C++ 68000 interpreter, executable loaders and host OS-service implementations. README and cpm/m.sh show original Digital Research compiler/assembler/linker stages being invoked through m68; MT Pascal, CB68 BASIC, DDT, SVS tools and Forth examples are documented uses of this one runner. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: 45b0c7378c7adc4433141d33cf5dd119b9cca612. A tooling emulator and partial OS-API reimplementation, not recovered source for the guest compilers. load_cpm68k reads the 0x601a executable header, creates a basepage and relocates text/data/BSS; trap 2 implements BDOS and trap 3 BIOS, with host fopen/fread-backed files. Trap 0 handles supported Linux-style services and trap 15 Fondse-style calls. The direct-run path constructs runtime state without booting CP/M or loading a ROM. Root LICENSE dedicates the emulator work under CC0-1.0. Checked-in Digital Research, Manx/Aztec, SVS, Forth and other legacy tools/support files retain their own rights; CC0 does not relicense third-party binaries or libraries. The README explicitly says the DOS-hosted Aztec C68K distribution requires a DOS emulator such as davidly/ntvdm: that compiler is not itself a native m68 guest. ntvcm/ntvdm nested builds and RVOS/ARMOS are related independent runners, not aliases of m68. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: ZXCC — CP/M compiler and command-line tool runner
decisions.reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. Tony Nicholson’s ZXCC maintains John Elliott’s ZXCC 0.5.7 lineage. It loads original CP/M .COM/.CPM programs at 0x100 and runs Ian Collier’s Z80 interpreter, while wrappers such as zxc, zxas, zxlink, zxlibr and zxobjtohex adapt host arguments for existing compiler tools. The original release and this maintained repository are one project family, not separate records. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: c45e5065eca63dd045d60511a8b21ab7f567303a. Cross-development tooling executes original binaries with partial CP/M 2/3 API translation. The ED FE trap routes BDOS/BIOS calls to native C; CPMREDIR maps CP/M drives and FCB operations onto host files. Required bios.bin is the bundled tiny ZXCC-specific synthetic BIOS/BDOS shim, with Z80/bios.zsm source, not an original vendor ROM or full CP/M OS. Users separately supply HI-TECH or Digital Research compiler binaries, includes, libraries and overlays. The maintained source derives from John Elliott ZXCC and Ian Collier’s xz80 CPU. Root COPYING/LICENSE and CPU carry GPLv2/GPL-2.0-or-later terms; CPMIO/CPMREDIR contain GNU Library GPL v2-or-later notices. Preserve component terms and separately supplied HI-TECH/Digital Research tools’ licences. README discusses fixes shared with zxccp, yaze and Mark Ogden, but related emulators and compiler repositories are not extra aliases or newly counted runner records here. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: ntvcm — CP/M 8080/Z80 command-line runner
decisions.reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. NT Virtual CP/M Machine is a standalone C++ command-line runner for CP/M .COM tools. ntvcm.cxx loads a selected host file at guest 0x100, creates CP/M entry hooks and enters x80.cxx. README documents asm/load, Turbo Pascal, Aztec C, WordStar and many other tools; they are compatibility examples, not separately reconstructed projects. The current head has removed the former GDB/MI debugger-host mode, so it is not advertised as a current capability. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: be598f65c1b649f5250dcd6d8fef266b1b86413e. An emulator with native CP/M BDOS/file and console translation, an 8080/Z80 trace disassembler and optional per-PC CSV profiling. It executes original instructions and synthesizes BDOS/BIOS hooks rather than booting a CP/M disk or requiring an original ROM. Host fopen/fread/fwrite implement FCB file operations. Original guest tools must be supplied with their own overlays/data; this record is the runner, not a full disk/hardware emulator or compiler reconstruction. Root LICENSE is CC0-1.0 for the emulator work; third-party CP/M programs and support files are not relicensed. The bundled z80test-cpm port preserves Patrik Rak’s separate MIT-style upstream licence. davidly/cpm_compilers holds example toolchains, while m68/RVOS can serve as nested hosts; these are related projects, not this runner’s aliases. Explicit DCC-derived fixes in recent commits are recorded without merging DCC into this identity. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: ntvdm — 8086 DOS command-line executable runner
decisions.reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. David Lee’s NT Virtual DOS Machine is an independent portable 8086/text-mode DOS runner, distinct from Microsoft’s system NTVDM component. ntvdm.cxx loads .COM and MZ/ZM .EXE files, applies relocations and runs i8086.cxx. README documents direct console/script use of MASM, Link, Microsoft C, Turbo Pascal/C, QuickBasic and other legacy tools. Original test software is included but does not become reconstructed source or separate runner records. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: 0649657d912f23e60b32971d1c45653d48b440e3. Tooling combines an 8086 interpreter with partial DOS 3.00-style APIs, BIOS/text-console and selected interrupt behavior. The loader creates PSP/environment and synthetic interrupt stubs; DOS file calls use native host fopen/fread/fwrite and -r maps a host directory to C:. Original executables run without a booted DOS OS or vendor ROM in the normal path. Optional boot-sector loading does not establish a complete PC hardware emulator. Root LICENSE uses CC0-1.0 for emulator work. The repository’s Microsoft, Borland and other legacy compiler/editor/application binaries retain separate rights; CC0 does not relicense them or their runtime libraries. The runner is separate from Microsoft NTVDM, DOSBox and the author’s dos_compilers examples. Related m68/sparcos host-emulation paths are recorded as dependencies/compatibility contexts without duplicate projects or claims that these tools were independently run here. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: Thames — ISIS-II 8080/8085 command-line tool runner
decisions.reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. Mark Ogden’s maintained Thames source explicitly derives from John Elliott’s Thames 0.1.1. Elliott’s official page identifies an ISIS-II runner for the tools used to build CP/M3, and the maintained loader/interpreter confirm direct original-binary execution. Count the original tarball and enhanced fork as one lineage under ogdenpm/thames-src. CP/M3 is the build product of example guest tools, not the OS API being emulated. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: dd545328888b6e989c5975053372d97a36dc336f. Modern tooling executes linked ISIS-II Intel OMF images, often without file extensions. isis_load accepts module/start/data/end records, loads bytes and rejects unresolved relocation/external/library records. main creates synthetic MDS BIOS/ISIS trap stubs in RAM, loads the argv-selected tool and enters the interpreter. ISIS OPEN/CLOSE/READ/WRITE/SEEK/LOAD translate to host files through device mapping; the path needs original tools/support files but no original boot ROM or booted ISIS OS. John Elliott origin and Mark Ogden enhancements remain one Thames family. The interpreter has GPL-2.0-or-later headers and COPYING is GPLv2; several ISIS/loader files have GNU Library GPL v2-or-later notices, so preserve mixed component terms. Original Intel tools are separately licensed. Documentation recommends newer native-C ports for several tools; those execute recompiled source and must not be conflated with Thames running originals. The previous documentation-only hold is superseded by this pinned source audit. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

decisions.title: Puzzland — Amiga picture-puzzle source archive
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga games-only discovery. Daniel Owsiański's author release of Puzzland, his first commercial Amiga game. README identifies an Amiga 500 scrolling picture-piece puzzle and preserves source, image assets, Polish AmigaGuide instructions and an ADF. Sources/Puzzland.c and PuzFunsPL.h implement the actual selection/event loop, scoring, piece covers and Intuition drawing; this is substantive original game source rather than a download wrapper. Canonical root and subject aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and the 2031-root prior-review index; this is a new project lineage. Current default-branch tip is 61cb503c28687739511e472782b908a4f7032e69; the complete tree contains 70 entries. README explicitly says the author does not know how to rebuild the game on modern systems. Sources/makefile is a historical TempCFile-oriented fragment: its lc invocation is commented out, it links with Blink and depends on df1:/LIB:/OBJ: assigns, AssRoutine.o and prebuilt Puzzland.lib. C/assembly, object files, libraries, full/demo binaries and an ADF are preserved, but their presence does not prove a clean source build or byte identity. All build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Tripppin — Amiga board-game source archive
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga games-only discovery. Paul Kienitz's original Amiga implementation of the remembered commercial board game Tripppples, represented by the fourth-release README and matching Tripppin 4 window title. Board.c shuffles the arrow tiles; Trip.c implements legal moves, recursive move selection and a separate thinking task; Jrdobbs.c draws the board pieces. The 8-by-8 game, configurable difficulty, suggestions and undo are substantive native game code. Canonical root and subject aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and the 2031-root prior-review index; this is a new project lineage. Current default-branch tip is b2132ac57c4be74393b1020cc8585f5fe1b77147; the complete tree contains 10 entries. MAKEFILE says Aztec C 5.0+ only and requires custom II and INTU precompiled headers with Amiga headers, pragmas and prototypes. Trip.h includes Paul.h, which is absent from the current complete nine-file tree. The README even describes a historical omitted-Paul.h distribution issue; it does not supply the missing file today. Filenames also retain Amiga-era case assumptions. No clean modern rebuild was verified; all build/runtime/byte-exact flags remain null.

decisions.title: Miner — Amiga Minesweeper source archive
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga games-only discovery. Paul Kienitz's original 1994-95 Amiga Minesweeper implementation, dedicated to Jay Miner. README distinguishes its click-on-press behavior, sound and color from the contemporary Windows game. action.c contains minefield generation, reveal/chord and scoring logic; miner.c implements the Amiga interface. Source, a preserved executable, sampled sounds, image data and release-5 manual are included. miner.h says VERSION 6, but the manual identifies release 5; the review does not invent a published sixth release. Canonical root and subject aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and the 2031-root prior-review index; this is a new project lineage. Current default-branch tip is e7317a617b00accc6b42923e7cfaf334544a3471; the complete tree contains 62 entries. Aztec C makefile depends on custom II/INTU precompiled headers, and miner.h includes Paul.h, absent from the complete repository tree. The preserved executable therefore does not establish a complete clean rebuild. Default options select AUTOFLASH and FIDDLE_FONT; optional BIG_STACK may need 50K or more of stack, but is not the documented default or a whole-machine RAM minimum. VERSION 6 in the header versus release 5 in Miner.doc is retained as an archive-version ambiguity. All four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Lugi — text-adventure revival with Amiga port
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga games-only discovery. Jay Wilson and Paul Kienitz's 1980-81 text adventure revived by its authors as portable C. README describes randomized maps, limited real-time runs and command-driven puzzle play; lugi.c provides the main game/score structure and enumerates substantive command, world, parser and action modules. Much of the Pascal-to-C translation was done in the early 1990s but unfinished then. The current tree includes a concrete native Amiga build and executable alongside modern ports, all one Lugi lineage. Canonical root and subject aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and the 2031-root prior-review index; this is a new project lineage. Current default-branch tip is c0a722044f397d9f8ad6e7a30ee29307701dc098; the complete tree contains 53 entries. README documents platform-specific builds sharing C sources: Amiga supports Manx Aztec C rather than SAS/C; the Amiga makefile selects 16-bit ints, stack overflow checking and lc16. Windows supports MSVC/Open Watcom, while its TCC route is explicitly broken. MS-DOS uses Open Watcom; Unix has gcc/clang/tcc scripts and Emscripten builds wasm/JS. Prebuilt target binaries and upstream build reports are not independent verification. Optional web high scores additionally require MySQL/MariaDB and configured PHP pages; no credentials are read or reproduced in this review. All build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Besch — Amiga card-game source archive
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga games-only discovery. Michael D. Bayne's Besch, archived under repository name beschei-en. Repository metadata identifies an Amiga card game circa 1995; main.c's historical revision and screen title independently establish the game name/author/date. The tree includes main event handling, cards/decks/stacks, move scoring, board logic and a computer opponent. These are substantial original C game modules, not merely screenshots or an executable wrapper. Canonical root and subject aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and the 2031-root prior-review index; this is a new project lineage. Current default-branch tip is 07c6eb2e235808eb84f89b259f7cd34cda81efe3; the complete tree contains 37 entries. Historical Makefile uses SAS/C SC with SLink named as linker, Amiga Delete/Copy commands and SDK/library headers, with eleven game modules and generated prototype headers. SCOPTIONS uses Amiga-specific options and CPU=68020; source relies on chip, __far and register conventions. A present-day toolchain or adaptation is needed to assess a clean rebuild. No README or top-level LICENSE is present in the complete tree, and no local compilation/execution or original-binary comparison was performed. All four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Else We Get Mad! — original Amiga fighting-game source
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga game discovery. EWGM is the original Else We Get Mad! game engine written by alpine9000 for Amiga Wave, which supplied the art, concept, sound effects and music and released the game. This is one game project, with its asset/build support retained under the same repository root. The reviewed player.c contains eight-direction joystick motion, attack-button/jump handling and punch/kick configuration, while the Makefile enumerates enemy/fighter logic and four level modules. It is substantive native game source, rather than a generic example or an asset-only archive. The inspected recipe uses developer-specific /usr/local/amiga/vgcc paths, the Amiga NDK, GCC-to-vasm assembly, vlink, a locally built libgcc archive, generated asset headers and shared external tools. It provides adf, fast and Workbench routes, with default all selecting fast and wb. Test recipes depend on the developer's FS-UAE folders and Lua setup; their presence is not a test result. No compiler, assembler, packer, emulator or game was executed in this review. All four build flags remain null, including byte exactness; source publication and the author's release statement do not prove a reproducible reconstruction.

decisions.title: OpenDOW — Dogs of War Amiga-game reimplementation
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga game discovery. OpenDOW is rofl0r's reimplementation of the 1989 Amiga Dogs of War, identified by the current repository description and original-resource credits. spriteview.c is the game executable despite its provisional name: it maintains player weapons, ammunition, scores and cash, enemies, projectiles, explosions, vehicles, collisions, mission transitions and map completion. It is counted once with its spawn editor and data. The title refers to the Amiga game actually reconstructed; other historical platform editions are not included merely because they share the name. README requires POSIX C99, Perl and SDL headers/libraries, plus sibling libulz, c-flod and rcb2 checkouts and a config.mak audio-backend define. The inspected Makefile defaults to a debug rcb2 build and provides optimized alternatives. These are recipes only; no candidate code or build tools were run. Gameplay remains incomplete: README lists dying as unfinished and says only Australia's spawn routes were authored. Current spawnmaps.c adds a Russia array still marked FIXME and maps ten other missions to Australia. This is stronger, current evidence than repeating the older README unchanged. All compilable/runnable/playable/byte_exact flags remain null.

decisions.title: The Financial Time Machine — Amiga source recovery and SDL reconstruction
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga game discovery. This repository preserves and adapts the 1985 Amiga The Financial Time Machine source release after loss of lessee6.c. The November 2014 README explicitly describes reconstructing missing functionality and replacing the backend for modern systems. ftm.c retains the financial-game model, stock/timeline logic, player portfolios, command handling and save/load behavior with local SDL-backed drawing/input replacements. The historical 1982 Odyssey 2 and later C64 editions are mentioned as ancestry only; this repository's actual source basis is the Amiga C release, so they are not additional source-platform records. README documents a C99 compiler, SDL and make; Makefile compiles the C files and links -lSDL, and no build/run was attempted. ftm.c explicitly defines warning-returning STUB bodies for calc_taxes, earnings_display, click, add_purchase and del_purchase. The active validity_check can emit UNHANDLED COMMAND GIVEN; the recovered validity_check_original is not the active implementation. A net-worth FIXME is also retained. These defects prevent any claim of complete restored gameplay. All four build flags remain null: neither a recipe, a large source file nor the recovered historical fragment verifies compilation, runtime, playability or binary identity.

decisions.title: Windless Bay — original Amiga interactive-fiction game
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga game discovery. Windless Bay is a distinct short interactive-fiction game set at an Antarctic research station near Mount Erebus. README identifies a classic-Amiga game built on R-Page, and game/game/world.c contains game-specific room/world state, CABLE plus COMBINE to TELEPHONE object combination, sprite associations and scenario conditions. The Makefile composes world, scene, GUI, text, assets and special-game modules with R-Page. Its world and content establish a game project beyond an engine checkout or screenshot repository. It is tracked separately from the existing rpage-resistance engine record. The inspected SAS/C recipe compiles native C objects, builds an includes.gst header and links main.exe with R-Page, AmigaOS and decompression components. Resource generation is a separate asset/scenario stage. The latest five commits explicitly include draft resource toolchain, draft content and draft navigation before fixes to PNG conversion and world.json navigation. A checked-in main.exe or resource pack does not establish a reproducible source build or a completed story. No tools or candidate binary were executed, and compilable, runnable, playable and byte_exact remain null. The catalogue preserves this as substantial but draft game work.

decisions.title: Soeki / Networ — partial Amiga/BeOS RTS source recovery
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga game discovery. Soeki, initially Networ and later also The Plague, is Lukas Hartmann's abandoned 1998–2000 real-time strategy game. README describes its Amiga 1200/Maxon C++ beginnings, move to BeOS and eventual loss of sources/assets. A friend retained only some of them and returned that partial archive years later. Amiga nw01/nw_light0, BeOS soeki_dev variants and sdl_port are one continuous game lineage. Reviewed SDL processing.cpp contains unit path tables, movement, attacks and deaths; Amiga source contains native screen/input/rendering work. The presence of real gameplay source is established without claiming a complete original restoration. This is an incomplete recovered archive, not a complete release-ready source restoration. Amiga code depends on period compiler/API assumptions and hard-coded TEXT:Hisoft_C paths, data files and assembly helpers. The inspected BeOS makefile depends on BUILDHOME/etc/makefile-engine and period /boot libraries/headers. The SDL script compiles the platform and independent C++ modules with g++ and links SDL2/SDL2_image. The 2019 commit reports an unfinished engine that runs, followed by 2020 header/output-name fixes; it is not independent test proof. None of the variants was built or executed here and all four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Burn — native Amiga side-scrolling shooter
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga-game discovery. Burn is RiPpEr253's source-available AmiGameJam2025 side-scrolling action/shooter. The inspected 68k source implements one/two-player selection, joystick motion, firing, jumping, enemies at nine scrolling checkpoints, health, knockback, invulnerability, score, respawning and shared lives. Burn executable and BurnAGJ25.adf are present in the 107-entry non-truncated tree but were only inventoried; source/binary correspondence is unverified. The provided .vscode/tasks.json uses the Amiga Assembly integration, vasm and vlink with src/rippergame.s as entry; source includes and assets are committed. This is a recipe, not a successful local compilation. The committed executable and ADF were not run or compared with source, and the author reports OS3.2.2 instability. All four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Battle Squadron 2 — Amiga Game Jam shooter source
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga-game discovery. Battle Squadron 2 is the bitwise-brains Amiga Game Jam 2024 shooter source. Its 2621-line game.c and related state/data headers implement four stages including a boss, enemy waves, player/enemy projectiles, collisions, damage, powerups, lives, special weapon, score table, intermissions and victory/loop states. The 47-entry non-truncated tree and sole Initial commit were inspected; this is one game rather than a template or four separate stages. CMake >=3.14 and C11 require an Amiga C compiler/toolchain, ACE and ace_audio_mixer. .gitmodules names AmigaPorts/ACE and CMake calls add_subdirectory(ace), but the complete snapshot has no ace directory or mode-160000 gitlink. A recursive clone alone cannot recover a pinned ACE dependency. The external cross-toolchain module path is ../../AmigaCMakeCrossToolchains/Modules/m68k-amigaos. file(COPY "${RES_DIR}/*" ...) is a suspicious literal-wildcard packaging line, not a reproduced build failure. No build or release binary was verified; all four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Amiga Games — Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader collection
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga-game discovery. amiga_games is one source-available AmigaBridge game collection with its own canonical root, distinct from the already-tracked parent tooling. Three inspected anchors establish the bounded game collection: Dot Chase implements maze dot-eating, ghost states, power pellets, fruit, score, lives and level completion; Fractalus implements terrain flight, pilot rescue/deception, landing/airlock/takeoff, combat, fuel/shield win/loss and attract mode; Void Trader implements space combat, docking, station trading, cargo/credits, salvage and win/game-over states. Void Trader prices are fixed with 90% resale; variable-price trade routes remain future work. The complete 426-entry tree was inspected and three game anchors were read in depth; this is not a claim that every listed game or asset was audited. The three per-game Makefiles require the external parent AmigaBridge headers and libbridge.a at ../../amiga-bridge, so the game repository alone is insufficient without that layout, dependency and matching compiler/library architecture. Classic builds use -noixemul; the two PPC branches use newlib and architecture-specific audio stubs. Fractalus/Void Trader treat failed ab_init as optional at runtime, so a running host MCP/daemon is not established as universally required merely by README deployment instructions. Dot Chase ignores that return value; daemon-free execution remains unverified. Parent examples-pin mismatch is retained under relationships. No collection build, binary availability or playthrough was independently verified; all four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Ermentrud / Inga — original Amiga adventure engine and SDL2 reimplementation
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga-game discovery. Ermentrud / Inga is one adventure-game/engine lineage spanning the preserved native AmigaOS3 engine and the modern Inga SDL reimplementation. README says Ermentrud and original Inga were created in 2001–2004 and the game was never finished. That origin does not date the later reimplementation. The original C engine has graphics, animation, actors, inventory, dialogues, bytecode execution and audio; the modern code has game state, navigation, scripts, scenes, menus and sound. inga-sdl is the canonical tracked root; inga-amigaos3 is an original-engine source alias, not a second project. The original engine has GCC and VBCC build recipes; VBCC selects +aos68k -cpu=68020. Modern CMake requires >=3.16.3 and SDL2, SDL2_mixer and SDL2_ttf; documented platform recipes additionally specify their SDK/dependencies. Separate Makefile.amigaos4 and Makefile.mos exist, but README says make -f Makefile.os4, a filename mismatch. Full Ermentrud game art/story/audio data are not the small Workshop sample committed with the engine; released game packages must be handled separately. No clean build, original/modern runtime, compatibility or byte comparison was performed, so all four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Original AmigaOS3 Inga engine — Ermentrud lineage alias
decisions.reason: Preserved original-engine source belongs to the single Ermentrud/Inga lineage represented by inga-sdl. Keep its 68020/RTG configuration and separate licensing evidence, but do not count another project.

decisions.title: BitRiot — desktop SDL2 reimplementation of Amiga Bug Bomber
decisions.reason: Approved Amiga-game discovery. BitRiot is a C++ clone/reimplementation of the Amiga game Bug Bomber. README traces it to a university project originally using Win32/DirectDraw, later ported to SDL1 and then SDL2; THANKS names Ross Turner for the initial game. The older tags and current SDL2 master are one project. Inspected GameEngine.cpp and the entity/player/spawn architecture establish substantial game implementation, not extracted Amiga original code. CMake >=3.4.3 selects C++14 and requires SDL2/mixer/ttf/image, OpenGL and RmlUi, with FreeType on the non-MinGW path. README asks for a recursive clone. .gitmodules and the tree pin mikke89/RmlUi under ext/RmlUi/RmlUi at 76245e8d615e5771ab6dd01ac4ea3c59038e6071; the build expects dependency outputs under ext/RmlUi, so the dependency build/layout is part of reproduction. Current CMake defaults to Release/static RmlUi; its Debug path explicitly reports unresolved static-RmlUi/FreeType linking issues. No clean build or execution was performed, and all four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: AmIga Minesweeper — native Amiga homebrew source
decisions.reason: Approved games-only publication. Darren Banfi’s AmIga Minesweeper is a distinct original native Amiga implementation, with source, screenshot and author README rather than an emulator wrapper or a mirror of another Minesweeper source release. The full minesweeper.c defines a 10-by-10 board with ten mines, adjacency counts, a queue-based empty-area reveal, flagging, mouse events, reset, win/loss handling and Amiga Intuition graphics/audio effects. It is not the same code lineage as Paul Kienitz’s Miner, despite sharing the game genre. The author’s root and title were absent from the current 1715 catalogue, source and decision indexes and 2031 prior-root union. README provides an m68k-amigaos GCC command and mentions VBCC; the tree contains source and screenshot rather than a verified generated binary/release. The implementation uses C99-style loops and modern Amiga SDK declarations, so exact compiler/SDK compatibility requires a future clean build. No build, installation, game execution, gameplay or byte comparison was performed, and all four build flags remain null. README’s fully-functional description is an author assertion, not an independent test.

decisions.title: Battleship — native AmigaOS 3 game source
decisions.reason: Approved games-only publication. This distinct native AmigaOS 3 C implementation has full, light and own-screen Battleship variants. The reviewed complete own-screen source implements ship placement/rotation/undo, player and computer shooting, hit counts, new game and terminal win/loss states; packaged LhA files and artwork are also present. The project is counted once across these variants. Its canonical tickBit/Amiga-Battleship root and subject-code identity do not match prior-reviewed roots or a current catalogue record. README requires VBCC with -c99 and says its backfill-hook implementation prevents direct use of other compilers. The checked-in source provides the own-screen compile line with -fpu=68881. C files and packed LhA binary distributions exist, but their correspondence and a clean rebuild were not tested. The README warns resource/library/allocation failures may behave badly. These are documented build/source facts, not observed compilation or playability; all four build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Tapper DOS reverse-engineering workspace
decisions.reason: The pinned five-file tree has a one-line README, TAPCOM.COM/TAPPER.EXE and two IDA .i64 databases, but no text reconstruction/build recipe. Binary/IDA analysis was outside this source-evidence lane; hold until inspectable reconstruction scope, provenance and asset/build requirements can be established. The C64 Tapper patch collection in the catalogue is a different platform lineage.

decisions.title: Vortexion Python/Pyxel shooter
decisions.reason: README explicitly says MSX/SG-1000-inspired Python/Pyxel game, requiring Python 3.7+ and Pyxel 2.0.13+. The complete tree contains Python game code, not an SG-1000/MSX native port or legacy-binary reconstruction. Excluded from this bounded native DOS/retro-console lane; this is not a judgment that the game is incomplete.

decisions.title: ucosty/blobbo
decisions.reason: Data-format reverse engineering and a level decoder/viewer only. The inspected BlobboGame class loads/decrypts levels; no playable game reconstruction or explicit 68k CPU proof was established. Keep as tooling context, not a game discovery.

decisions.title: kainjow/Glypha
decisions.reason: Modern port in the same Glypha III source lineage as the original softdorothy/Glypha3 archive selected in this batch; do not double-count the port as another discovered family.

decisions.title: sp00nznet/macrecomp
decisions.reason: Reusable static-recompilation/Toolbox toolkit and dependency rather than a game; record runtime boundary as evidence for Shufflepuck, without adding a separate game row.

decisions.title: scottschiller/ArmorAlley
decisions.reason: Substantial browser game was identified, but this bounded pass did not finish independent primary proof for exact historical 68k support, asset licensing and implementation lineage. Unpromoted lead, not rejected as ineligible.

decisions.title: PangeaSoftware/MightyMike
decisions.reason: Repository metadata exists, but its advertised master branch returned Branch not found. No readable source tree established in this route; do not infer 68k from classic Mac description.

decisions.title: softdorothy/GliderPRO
